saguṇaṃ nirguṇaṃ brahma staumi svecchāsvarūpiṇam..
sarvendriyādidevaṃ tamindriyālayameva ca ..44..
4.20.d:
सगुणं निर्गुणं ब्रह्म स्तौमि स्वेच्छास्वरूपिणम्॥
सर्वेन्द्रियादिदेवं तमिन्द्रियालयमेव च ॥44॥
4.20.m:
I praise Brahman, with qualities and without qualities, whose form is his own will,
the primal deity of all the senses, and the abode of the senses. (44)

4.20.s:
sarvendriyasvarūpaṃ ca virāḍrūpaṃ namāmyaham ..
vedaṃ ca vedajanakaṃ sarvavedāṅgarūpiṇam..45..
4.20.d:
सर्वेन्द्रियस्वरूपं च विराड्रूपं नमाम्यहम् ॥
वेदं च वेदजनकं सर्ववेदाङ्गरूपिणम्॥45॥
4.20.m:
I bow to the one whose form is all the senses, who has the form of Virāj,
the Veda and the progenitor of the Veda, embodying all limbs of the Veda. (45)

4.20.s:
sarvamantasvarūpaṃ ca namāmi parameśvaram ..
sārātsārataraṃ dravyamapūrvamanirūpiṇam .. 46 ..
4.20.d:
सर्वमन्तस्वरूपं च नमामि परमेश्वरम् ॥
सारात्सारतरं द्रव्यमपूर्वमनिरूपिणम् ॥ 46 ॥
4.20.m:
I bow to the Supreme Lord, whose form is the end of all,
the reality more essential than the essence, unprecedented and indefinable. (46)

4.20.s:
svatantramasvatantraṃ ca yaśodānandanaṃ bhaje ..
santaṃ sarvaśarīreṣu tamadṛṣṭamanūhakam ..47..
4.20.d:
स्वतन्त्रमस्वतन्त्रं च यशोदानन्दनं भजे ॥
सन्तं सर्वशरीरेषु तमदृष्टमनूहकम् ॥47॥
4.20.m:
I worship the son of Yaśodā, who is independent and dependent,
existing in all bodies, unseen and inconceivable. (47)

4.20.s:
dhyānāsādhyaṃ vidyamānaṃ yogīndrāṇāṃ guruṃ bhaje ..
rāsamaṇḍalamadhyasthaṃ rāsollāsasamutsukam ..48..
4.20.d:
ध्यानासाध्यं विद्यमानं योगीन्द्राणां गुरुं भजे ॥
रासमण्डलमध्यस्थं रासोल्लाससमुत्सुकम् ॥48॥
4.20.m: Inaccessible by meditation yet present, I worship the guru of the kings of yogins,

4.20.s:
gopībhiḥ sevyamānaṃ ca taṃ dhareśaṃ namāmyaham ..
satāṃ sadaiva santaṃ tamasantamasatāmapi..49..
4.20.d:
गोपीभिः सेव्यमानं च तं धरेशं नमाम्यहम् ॥
सतां सदैव सन्तं तमसन्तमसतामपि॥49॥
4.20.m:
served by the cowherd women; I bow to that Lord of the earth,
always present to the good, yet nonexistent even to the wicked. (49)

4.20.s:
yogīśaṃ yogasādhyaṃ ca namāmi śivasevitam..
mantrabījaṃ mantrarājaṃ mantradaṃ phaladaṃ phalam .. ..4.20.50..
4.20.d:
योगीशं योगसाध्यं च नमामि शिवसेवितम्॥
मन्त्रबीजं मन्त्रराजं मन्त्रदं फलदं फलम् ॥ ॥4.20.50॥
4.20.m:
I bow to the Lord of yoga, attainable through yoga, served by Śiva,
the seed of mantras, king of mantras, giver of mantras, giver of fruits, the fruit itself, (50)

4.20.s:
mantrasiddhisvarūpaṃ taṃ namāmi ca parātparam ..
sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ ca sukhadaṃ duḥkhadaṃ puṇyameva ca ..51..
4.20.d:
मन्त्रसिद्धिस्वरूपं तं नमामि च परात्परम् ॥
सुखं दुःखं च सुखदं दुःखदं पुण्यमेव च ॥51॥
4.20.m:
whose form is the perfection of mantras; and I bow to him who is higher than the highest,
pleasure and pain, the giver of pleasure, the giver of pain, and virtue itself. (51)

4.20.s:
puṇyapradaṃ ca śubhadaṃ śubhabījaṃ namāmyaham ..
ityevaṃ stavanaṃ kṛtvā dattvā gāśca sa bālakān .. 92 ..
4.20.d:
पुण्यप्रदं च शुभदं शुभबीजं नमाम्यहम् ॥
इत्येवं स्तवनं कृत्वा दत्त्वा गाश्च स बालकान् ॥ 92 ॥
4.20.m:
The bestower of merit, the giver of good, the seed of auspiciousness—I bow [to him].
Having offered praise in this way and returned the cows and the boys, (52)

4.20.s:
nipatya daṇḍavadbhūmau ruroda praṇanāma ca ..
dadarśa cakṣurunmīlya vidhātā jagatāṃ mune .. 53 ..
4.20.d:
निपत्य दण्डवद्भूमौ रुरोद प्रणनाम च ॥
ददर्श चक्षुरुन्मील्य विधाता जगतां मुने ॥ 53 ॥
4.20.m:
falling like a rod upon the ground, he wept and bowed down.
Opening his eyes, O sage, the Creator of the worlds looked. (53)

4.20.s:
brahmaṇā ca kṛtaṃ stotraṃ nityaṃ bhaktyā ca yaḥ paṭhet ..
iha loke sukhaṃ bhuktvā yātyante śrīhareḥ padam .. 54 ..
4.20.d:
ब्रह्मणा च कृतं स्तोत्रं नित्यं भक्त्या च यः पठेत् ॥
इह लोके सुखं भुक्त्वा यात्यन्ते श्रीहरेः पदम् ॥ 54 ॥
4.20.m: Whoever recites daily with devotion this hymn of praise composed by Brahmā,

4.20.s:
labhate dāsyamatulaṃ sthānamīśvarasannidhau ..
labdhvā ca kṛṣṇasānnidhyaṃ pārṣadapravaro bhavet .. 55 ..
4.20.d:
लभते दास्यमतुलं स्थानमीश्वरसन्निधौ ॥
लब्ध्वा च कृष्णसान्निध्यं पार्षदप्रवरो भवेत् ॥ 55 ॥
4.20.m:
He obtains incomparable servitude and a place in the presence of the Lord;
and having attained the proximity of Kṛṣṇa, he becomes the foremost of his attendants. (55)

4.20.s:
śrīnārāyaṇa uvāca ..
gate jagatkāraṇe ca brahmalokaṃ ca brahmaṇi ..
śrīkṛṣṇo bālakaiḥ sārdhaṃ jagāma svālayaṃ vibhuḥ .. 56 ..
4.20.d:
श्रीनारायण उवाच ॥
गते जगत्कारणे च ब्रह्मलोकं च ब्रह्मणि ॥
श्रीकृष्णो बालकैः सार्धं जगाम स्वालयं विभुः ॥ 56 ॥
4.20.m:
When Brahmā, the cause of the world, had gone to Brahmaloka,
the all-pervading Śrī Kṛṣṇa went to his own abode along with the boys. (56)

4.20.s:
gāvo vatsāśca bālāśca jagmurvarṣāntare gṛham ..
śrīkṛṣṇamāyayā sarve menire te dināntaram .. 57 ..
4.20.d:
गावो वत्साश्च बालाश्च जग्मुर्वर्षान्तरे गृहम् ॥
श्रीकृष्णमायया सर्वे मेनिरे ते दिनान्तरम् ॥ 57 ॥
4.20.m:
The cows, the calves, and the boys returned home after a year;
by the māyā of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, they all considered it to be [just] another day. (57)

4.20.s:
gopā gopālikā kiṃcittatkartuṃ na kṣamāstadā ..
yoginaḥ kṛtrimaṃ sarvaṃ kiṃ nūtnaṃ vā purātanam .. 58 ..
4.20.d:
गोपा गोपालिका किंचित्तत्कर्तुं न क्षमास्तदा ॥
योगिनः कृत्रिमं सर्वं किं नूत्नं वा पुरातनम् ॥ 58 ॥
4.20.m:
The cowherds and cowherd women were not able to understand that at all.
To the yogin, all is artificial: what is new or what is ancient? (58)

4.20.s:
ityevaṃ kathitaṃ sarvaṃ śrīkṛṣṇacaritaṃ śubham ..
sukhadaṃ mokṣadaṃ puṇyaṃ sarvakālasukhāvaham .. 59 ..
4.20.d:
इत्येवं कथितं सर्वं श्रीकृष्णचरितं शुभम् ॥
सुखदं मोक्षदं पुण्यं सर्वकालसुखावहम् ॥ 59 ॥
4.20.m:
Thus all the auspicious acts of Śrī Kṛṣṇa have been told,
bestowing happiness, giving liberation, meritorious, bringing joy at all times. (59)

4.21.s:
śrīnārāyaṇa uvāca ..
ekadā''nandayuktaśca nando gopavraje mune ..
dundubhiṃ vādayāmāsa śakrayāgakṛtodyamaḥ .. 1 ..
4.21.d:
श्रीनारायण उवाच ॥
एकदा'ऽनन्दयुक्तश्च नन्दो गोपव्रजे मुने ॥
दुन्दुभिं वादयामास शक्रयागकृतोद्यमः ॥ 1 ॥
4.21.m: Śrī Nārāyaṇa said: / Once, filled with joy in the cowherd settlement of Vraja, O sage, / Nanda had the kettle-drums sounded, having undertaken the sacrifice to Indra: (1) / 'Curd, milk, clarified butter, buttermilk, butter, molasses, honey— / taking these, perform the worship of Indra!' he said. (2) / 'Whoever there are here in this town—cowherds, cowherd women, boys, / girls, twice-born, and also vaiśyas and śūdras—with devotion.' (3) / Thus he proclaimed himself, full of joy. / He raised a pole in a charming, very wide place; (4) / he gave there silken cloth, a delightful mass of garlands, / sandalwood, aguru, musk, and saffron paste. (5) / Bathed, having performed his daily rites with devotion, wearing two clean garments, / he sat on a golden seat, his lotus feet washed, (6) / with various kinds of vessels, and with brāhmaṇas and family priests, / cowherds and cowherd women, girls together with boys. (7) / In the meantime, the townspeople came there, / with great collections of provisions gathered, bringing various offerings. (8) / All the sages came, blazing with the splendour of Brahman, / tranquil, together with multitudes of disciples, masters of the Vedas and Vedāṅgas: (9) / Garga, Gālava, Śākalya, Śākaṭāyana, / Gautama, Karuṣa, Kaṇva, Vātsya, and Kātyāyana, (10) / Saubhari, Vāmadeva, Yājñavalkya, Pāṇini, / Ṛṣyaśṛṅga, Gauramukha, Bharadvāja, Vāmana, (11) / Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana, Śṛṅgin, Sumantu, Jaimini, Kaca, / Parāśara, Maitreya, and Vaiśampāyana. (12) / And various kinds of brāhmaṇas, mendicants, bards, / kings, vaiśyas, and śūdras assembled at the great festival. (13) / Seeing the foremost of sages, the brāhmaṇas, and the rulers of the earth, Nanda / rose from his golden seat, and the people of Vraja rose as well. (14) / Having bowed, he seated the foremost of sages, the brāhmaṇas, and the kings.

4.21.s:
dadhi kṣīraṃ ghṛtaṃ takraṃ navanītaṃ guḍaṃ madhu ..
etānyādāya śakrasya pūjāṃ kurvantviti bruvan ..2..
4.21.d:
दधि क्षीरं घृतं तक्रं नवनीतं गुडं मधु ॥
एतान्यादाय शक्रस्य पूजां कुर्वन्त्विति ब्रुवन् ॥2॥

4.21.s:
yeye santyatra nagare gopā gopyaśca bālakāḥ ..
bālikāśca dvijā bhūyo vaiśyāḥ śūdrāśca bhaktitaḥ .. 3 ..
4.21.d:
येये सन्त्यत्र नगरे गोपा गोप्यश्च बालकाः ॥
बालिकाश्च द्विजा भूयो वैश्याः शूद्राश्च भक्तितः ॥ 3 ॥

4.21.s:
ityevaṃ śrāvayāmāsa svayameva mudā'nvitaḥ ..
yaṣṭimāropayāmāsa ramyasthāne suvistṛte .. 4 ..
4.21.d:
इत्येवं श्रावयामास स्वयमेव मुदाऽन्वितः ॥
यष्टिमारोपयामास रम्यस्थाने सुविस्तृते ॥ 4 ॥

4.21.s:
dadau tatra kṣaumavastraṃ mālājālaṃ manoharam ..
candanāgurukastūrīkuṅkumadravameva ca .. 5 ..
4.21.d:
ददौ तत्र क्षौमवस्त्रं मालाजालं मनोहरम् ॥
चन्दनागुरुकस्तूरीकुङ्कुमद्रवमेव च ॥ 5 ॥

4.21.s:
snātaḥ kṛtāhniko bhaktyā dhṛtvā dhaute ca vāsasī..
uvāsa svarṇapīṭhe ca prakṣālitapadāmbujaḥ ..6..
4.21.d:
स्नातः कृताह्निको भक्त्या धृत्वा धौते च वाससी॥
उवास स्वर्णपीठे च प्रक्षालितपदाम्बुजः ॥6॥

4.21.s:
nānāprakārapātraiśca brāhmaṇaiśca purohitaiḥ ..
gopālairgopikābhiśca bālābhiḥ saha bālakaiḥ .. 7 ..
4.21.d:
नानाप्रकारपात्रैश्च ब्राह्मणैश्च पुरोहितैः ॥
गोपालैर्गोपिकाभिश्च बालाभिः सह बालकैः ॥ 7 ॥

4.21.s:
etasminnantare tatrājagmurnagaravāsinaḥ ..
mahāsaṃbhṛtasaṃbhārā nānopāyanasaṃyutāḥ .. 8 ..
4.21.d:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे तत्राजग्मुर्नगरवासिनः ॥
महासंभृतसंभारा नानोपायनसंयुताः ॥ 8 ॥

4.21.s:
ājagmurmunayaḥ sarve jvalantaṃ brahmatejasā ..
śāntāḥ śiṣyagaṇaiḥ sārdhaṃ vedavedāṅgapāragāḥ .. 9 ..
4.21.d:
आजग्मुर्मुनयः सर्वे ज्वलन्तं ब्रह्मतेजसा ॥
शान्ताः शिष्यगणैः सार्धं वेदवेदाङ्गपारगाः ॥ 9 ॥

4.21.s:
gargaśca gālavaścaiva śākalyaḥ śākaṭāyanaḥ ..
gautamaḥ karuṣaḥ kaṇvo vātsyaḥ kātyāyanastathā .. 4.21.10 ..
4.21.d:
गर्गश्च गालवश्चैव शाकल्यः शाकटायनः ॥
गौतमः करुषः कण्वो वात्स्यः कात्यायनस्तथा ॥ 4.21.10 ॥

4.21.s:
saubharirvāmadevaśca yājñavalkyaśca pāṇiniḥ ..
ṛṣyaśṛṅgo gauramukho bharadvājaśca vāmanaḥ ..11..
4.21.d:
सौभरिर्वामदेवश्च याज्ञवल्क्यश्च पाणिनिः ॥
ऋष्यशृङ्गो गौरमुखो भरद्वाजश्च वामनः ॥11॥

4.21.s:
kṛṣṇadvaipāyanaḥ śṛṅgī sumanturjaiminiḥ kacaḥ ..
parāśaraśca maitreyo vaiśampāyana eva ca .. 12 ..
4.21.d:
कृष्णद्वैपायनः शृङ्गी सुमन्तुर्जैमिनिः कचः ॥
पराशरश्च मैत्रेयो वैशम्पायन एव च ॥ 12 ॥

4.21.s:
brāhmaṇāśca katividhā bhikṣukā bandinastathā ..
bhūpā vaiśyāśca śūdrāśca samājagmurmahotsave .. 13 ..
4.21.d:
ब्राह्मणाश्च कतिविधा भिक्षुका बन्दिनस्तथा ॥
भूपा वैश्याश्च शूद्राश्च समाजग्मुर्महोत्सवे ॥ 13 ॥

4.21.s:
dṛṣṭvā munīndrānnandaśca brāhmaṇānbhūmipāṃstathā ..
svarṇapīṭhātsamuttasthau vrajāścottasthureva ca.. 14 ..
4.21.d:
दृष्ट्वा मुनीन्द्रान्नन्दश्च ब्राह्मणान्भूमिपांस्तथा ॥
स्वर्णपीठात्समुत्तस्थौ व्रजाश्चोत्तस्थुरेव च॥ 14 ॥

4.21.s:
praṇamya vāsayāmāsa munīndrānviprabhūmipān ..
teṣāmanumatiṃ prāpya tatrovāsa punarmudā .. 15 ..
4.21.d:
प्रणम्य वासयामास मुनीन्द्रान्विप्रभूमिपान् ॥
तेषामनुमतिं प्राप्य तत्रोवास पुनर्मुदा ॥ 15 ॥

4.21.s:
pākaṃ ca yaṣṭinikaṭe kartumājñāṃ cakāra ha ..
pākaprājñaṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ śatamānīya sādaram .. 16 ..
4.21.d:
पाकं च यष्टिनिकटे कर्तुमाज्ञां चकार ह ॥
पाकप्राज्ञं ब्राह्मणानां शतमानीय सादरम् ॥ 16 ॥

4.21.s:
tatra ratnapradīpāśca jajvaluḥ paritastathā ..
andhībhūtaṃ ca dhūpena sthānaṃ tatsurabhīkṛtam .. 17 ..
4.21.d:
तत्र रत्नप्रदीपाश्च जज्वलुः परितस्तथा ॥
अन्धीभूतं च धूपेन स्थानं तत्सुरभीकृतम् ॥ 17 ॥

4.21.s:
nānāvidhāni puṣpāṇi mālyāni vividhāni ca ..
naivedyaṃ ca bahuvidhamapūrvaṃ sumanoharam .. 18 ..
4.21.d:
नानाविधानि पुष्पाणि माल्यानि विविधानि च ॥
नैवेद्यं च बहुविधमपूर्वं सुमनोहरम् ॥ 18 ॥

4.21.s:
tilalaḍḍukapūrṇaṃ ca maṇḍakānāṃ sahasrakam ..
svastikaiḥ paripūrṇaṃ ca yaṣṭisthānaṃ ca nārada .. 19 ..
4.21.d:
तिललड्डुकपूर्णं च मण्डकानां सहस्रकम् ॥
स्वस्तिकैः परिपूर्णं च यष्टिस्थानं च नारद ॥ 19 ॥

4.21.s:
kalaśānāṃ sahasraṃ ca pūrṇaṃ śarkarayā mune ..
yavagodhūmacūrṇānāṃ laḍḍukairmadhurairvaraiḥ ..4.21.20..
4.21.d:
कलशानां सहस्रं च पूर्णं शर्करया मुने ॥
यवगोधूमचूर्णानां लड्डुकैर्मधुरैर्वरैः ॥4.21.20॥

4.21.s:
ghṛtapakvairviprakṛtaiḥ pūrṇāni kalaśāni ca ..
vṛkṣapakvāni ramyāṇi cārurambhāphalāni ca ..21..
4.21.d:
घृतपक्वैर्विप्रकृतैः पूर्णानि कलशानि च ॥
वृक्षपक्वानि रम्याणि चारुरम्भाफलानि च ॥21॥

4.21.s:
phalāni paripakvāni kāladeśodbhavāni ca..
kṣīrāṇāṃ kumbhalakṣāṇi dadhnāṃ tāvanti nārada .. 22 ..
4.21.d:
फलानि परिपक्वानि कालदेशोद्भवानि च॥
क्षीराणां कुम्भलक्षाणि दध्नां तावन्ति नारद ॥ 22 ॥

4.21.s:
madhūnāṃ kumbhaśatakaṃ sarpiṣkumbha sahasrakam ..
kalaśānāṃ trilakṣāṇi takrapūrṇāni niścitam .. 23 ..
4.21.d:
मधूनां कुम्भशतकं सर्पिष्कुम्भ सहस्रकम् ॥
कलशानां त्रिलक्षाणि तक्रपूर्णानि निश्चितम् ॥ 23 ॥

4.21.s:
ghaṭānāṃ pañcalakṣāṇi guḍapūrṇāni niścitam ..
tilatailena pūrṇaṃ ca kalaśānāṃ sahasrakam .. 24 ..
vṛṣendrāśca bahuvidhā bhogārhadravyavāhakāḥ ..
nānāvidhāni pātrāṇi sauvarṇarājatāni ca .. 29 ..
4.21.d:
घटानां पञ्चलक्षाणि गुडपूर्णानि निश्चितम् ॥
तिलतैलेन पूर्णं च कलशानां सहस्रकम् ॥ 24 ॥
वृषेन्द्राश्च बहुविधा भोगार्हद्रव्यवाहकाः ॥
नानाविधानि पात्राणि सौवर्णराजतानि च ॥ 29 ॥

4.21.s:
svarṇapīṭhāni ca brahmannājagmuryaṣṭisannidhim ..
vastrāṇi varaṇārhāṇi cārūṇi bhūṣaṇāni ca .. 25 ..
4.21.d:
स्वर्णपीठानि च ब्रह्मन्नाजग्मुर्यष्टिसन्निधिम् ॥
वस्त्राणि वरणार्हाणि चारूणि भूषणानि च ॥ 25 ॥

4.21.s:
nānāvidhāni vādyāni cārūṇi madhurāṇi ca ..
vādakāḥ svarayantrāṇi vādayāmāsurutsave .. 27 ..
4.21.d:
नानाविधानि वाद्यानि चारूणि मधुराणि च ॥
वादकाः स्वरयन्त्राणि वादयामासुरुत्सवे ॥ 27 ॥

4.21.s:
chāgalānāṃ sahasrāṇi mahiṣāṇāṃ śatāni ca ..
meṣakāṇāṃ ca lakṣāṇi hyānayāmāsa tatra vai ..28..
4.21.d:
छागलानां सहस्राणि महिषाणां शतानि च ॥
मेषकाणां च लक्षाणि ह्यानयामास तत्र वै ॥28॥

4.21.s:
śatānyeva gaṇḍakānāmājagmuryaṣṭisaṃnidhim ..
prekṣitāni ca sarvāṇi rakṣitāni ca rakṣakaiḥ..29..
4.21.d:
शतान्येव गण्डकानामाजग्मुर्यष्टिसंनिधिम् ॥
प्रेक्षितानि च सर्वाणि रक्षितानि च रक्षकैः॥29॥

4.21.s:
bālakānāṃ bālikānāṃ vṛkṣāṇāṃ vṛkṣayoṣitām ..
yūnāṃ ca yuvatīnāṃ ca saṃkhyāṃ kartuṃ ca kaḥ kṣamaḥ ..4.21.30..
4.21.d:
बालकानां बालिकानां वृक्षाणां वृक्षयोषिताम् ॥
यूनां च युवतीनां च संख्यां कर्तुं च कः क्षमः ॥4.21.30॥

4.21.s:
gāyakānāṃ ca saṃgītaṃ nartakānāṃ ca nartanam ..
śrutvā dṛṣṭvā janāḥ sarve mumuhuḥ sumahotsave .. 31 ..
4.21.d:
गायकानां च संगीतं नर्तकानां च नर्तनम् ॥
श्रुत्वा दृष्ट्वा जनाः सर्वे मुमुहुः सुमहोत्सवे ॥ 31 ॥

4.21.s:
raṃbhorvaśī menakā ca ghṛtācī mohinī ratiḥ ..
prabhāvatī bhānumatī vipracittistilottamā .. 32 ..
4.21.d:
रंभोर्वशी मेनका च घृताची मोहिनी रतिः ॥
प्रभावती भानुमती विप्रचित्तिस्तिलोत्तमा ॥ 32 ॥

4.21.s:
candraprabhā suprabhā ca ratnamālā madālasā ..
reṇukā ramaṇī brahmannetā ājagmurutsave .. 33 ..
4.21.d:
चन्द्रप्रभा सुप्रभा च रत्नमाला मदालसा ॥
रेणुका रमणी ब्रह्मन्नेता आजग्मुरुत्सवे ॥ 33 ॥

4.21.s:
tāsāṃ nṛtyena gītena stanāsyaśroṇidarśanāt ..
rūpeṇa vakradṛṣṭyā ca mūrcchāṃ prāpuśca mānavāḥ .. 34 ..
4.21.d:
तासां नृत्येन गीतेन स्तनास्यश्रोणिदर्शनात् ॥
रूपेण वक्रदृष्ट्या च मूर्च्छां प्रापुश्च मानवाः ॥ 34 ॥

4.21.s:
etasminnantare śīghramājagāma hariḥ svayam ..
gopālabālakaiḥ sārdhaṃ balena balaśālinā..35..
4.21.d:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे शीघ्रमाजगाम हरिः स्वयम् ॥
गोपालबालकैः सार्धं बलेन बलशालिना॥35॥

4.21.s:
dṛṣṭvā taṃ ca janāḥ sarve saṃbhrāntā harṣavihvalāḥ ..
uttasthurārādbhītāśca pulakāṅkitavigrahāḥ .. 36..
4.21.d:
दृष्ट्वा तं च जनाः सर्वे संभ्रान्ता हर्षविह्वलाः ॥
उत्तस्थुराराद्भीताश्च पुलकाङ्कितविग्रहाः ॥ 36॥

4.21.s:
krīḍāsthānātsamāyāntaṃ śāntaṃ sundaravigraham..
vinodamuralīveṇuśṛṅgaśabdasamanvitam .. 37 ..
4.21.d:
क्रीडास्थानात्समायान्तं शान्तं सुन्दरविग्रहम्॥
विनोदमुरलीवेणुशृङ्गशब्दसमन्वितम् ॥ 37 ॥

4.21.s:
sadratnasārabhūṣābhirbhūṣitaṃ kaustubhena ca ..
candanāgurupaṅkena carcitaṃ śyāmavigraham .. 38 ..
4.21.d:
सद्रत्नसारभूषाभिर्भूषितं कौस्तुभेन च ॥
चन्दनागुरुपङ्केन चर्चितं श्यामविग्रहम् ॥ 38 ॥

4.21.s:
śaranmadhyāhnapadmāsyaṃ paśyantaṃ ratnadarpaṇe ..
cārucandanacandreṇa kastūrībindunā saha .. 39 ..
4.21.d:
शरन्मध्याह्नपद्मास्यं पश्यन्तं रत्नदर्पणे ॥
चारुचन्दनचन्द्रेण कस्तूरीबिन्दुना सह ॥ 39 ॥

4.21.s:
śaśāṅkena yathā''kāśaṃ bhālamadhyavirājitam ..
mālatīmālayā śyāmakaṇṭhavakṣaḥsthalojjvalam ..4.21.40..
4.21.d:
शशाङ्केन यथा'ऽकाशं भालमध्यविराजितम् ॥
मालतीमालया श्यामकण्ठवक्षःस्थलोज्ज्वलम् ॥4.21.40॥

4.21.s:
bakapaṅktyā yathā''kāśaṃ śāradīyaṃ sunirmalam..
cāruṇā pītavastreṇa śobhitaṃ śyāmavigraham ..41..
4.21.d:
बकपङ्क्त्या यथा'ऽकाशं शारदीयं सुनिर्मलम्॥
चारुणा पीतवस्त्रेण शोभितं श्यामविग्रहम् ॥41॥

4.21.s:
vibhāntaṃ vidyutā śaśvannavaniṃ nīradaṃ yathā ..
kundaprasūnairguñjābhirbaddhavakrimacūḍakam .. 42 ..
4.21.d:
विभान्तं विद्युता शश्वन्नवनिं नीरदं यथा ॥
कुन्दप्रसूनैर्गुञ्जाभिर्बद्धवक्रिमचूडकम् ॥ 42 ॥

4.21.s:
yathendradhanuṣā bhāti vibhātaṃ bhagaṇairnabhaḥ ..
ratnakuṇḍaladīptyā ca smitavaktrasuśobhitam .. 43 ..
4.21.d:
यथेन्द्रधनुषा भाति विभातं भगणैर्नभः ॥
रत्नकुण्डलदीप्त्या च स्मितवक्त्रसुशोभितम् ॥ 43 ॥

4.21.s:
śaratpraphullapadmaṃ ca dyumaṇeḥ kiraṇairyathā ..
viprakṣattriyavaiśyāśca munayo ballavā mune .. 44 ..
4.21.d:
शरत्प्रफुल्लपद्मं च द्युमणेः किरणैर्यथा ॥
विप्रक्षत्त्रियवैश्याश्च मुनयो बल्लवा मुने ॥ 44 ॥
4.21.m:
and of young men and young women, who indeed was capable of counting?
Hearing the singing of the singers and seeing the dancing of the dancers, / all the people were enchanted at that great festival.
Rambhā, Urvaśī, Menakā, Ghṛtācī, Mohinī, Rati, / Prabhāvatī, Bhānumatī, Vipracitti, Tilottamā,
Candraprabhā, Suprabhā, Ratnamālā, Madālasā, / Reṇukā, and Ramaṇī came to the festival, O Brahman.
From their dancing, singing, and the sight of their breasts, faces, and hips, / from their beauty and sidelong glances, the men swooned.
In the meantime, Hari himself came quickly, / along with the cowherd boys and the mighty Bala.
Seeing him, all the people, agitated and overwhelmed with joy, / stood up from afar in awe, their bodies bristling with hairs.
Coming from the playground, peaceful, of handsome form, / accompanied by the playful sound of flutes, reeds, and horns,
adorned with ornaments made of the essence of fine gems and with the Kaustubha, / his dark body anointed with sandal and aguru paste,
looking into a gem mirror with a face like an autumn midday lotus, / with a lovely moon of sandal together with a dot of musk,
which shone in the middle of his forehead as the moon shines in the sky; / resplendent at his dark neck and chest with a garland of mālatī flowers,
just as the very clear autumn sky [is adorned] by a flight of cranes; / his dark body adorned with a lovely yellow cloth,
shining continually like a fresh raincloud with lightning; / his curved crest tied with kunda blossoms and guñjā berries,
which shines as the morning sky with a host of stars shines with a rainbow; / his smiling face looking beautiful with the radiance of gem earrings,
like an autumn lotus in bloom [shining] with the rays of the sun— / brahmins, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, sages, and cowherds, O sage,

4.21.s:
praṇamya vāsayāmāsū ratnasiṃhāsane śubhe ..
uvāsa ratnapīṭhe sa teṣāṃ madhye jagatpatiḥ.. 45 ..
4.21.d:
प्रणम्य वासयामासू रत्नसिंहासने शुभे ॥
उवास रत्नपीठे स तेषां मध्ये जगत्पतिः॥ 45 ॥
4.21.m:
having bowed, seated him upon an auspicious throne of gems. / He, the Lord of the universe, sat upon that seat of gems in their midst,
just as the autumn moon shines in the sky amidst the heavenly bodies. / Having heard, they all spoke to him, the supreme Lord of the universes,
who acts according to his own will, beyond the gunas, whose nature is light, eternal. / Seeing the great festival, Hari, skilled in the science of conduct, / quickly spoke to his father words on conduct that are difficult for all to attain.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: / O king of cowherds, O observer of good vows, what are you doing here?
Who is to be worshipped, what is the worship, and what fruit might come from worshipping? / Or what means [is gained] by the fruit, and who is an ally through the means?
Or if the god is angered when there is an obstacle to worship, what would happen? / If pleased, what fruit does the god bestow here and in the hereafter?
One [worship] gives fruit here, but none in the hereafter; / another gives neither in both, and another in both.
Worship not prescribed by the Veda is a vessel causing total loss. / Is this worship of yours modern, or has it come down through generations of forebears?
In what [form] was the god seen by you, in accord with which this worship is conducted? / Does your god eat directly, or does he not eat directly?
That worship is highly praised where the god eats directly. / Janārdana in the form of a brahmin eats the food-offering directly.
When a brahmin is thoroughly pleased, all deities are pleased. / What use has he for the worship of gods, who is engaged in the worship of the twice-born?
By him who has worshipped brahmins, all deities have been worshipped. / Having offered the food-offering to the god, if one does not give it to the twice-born,
the food-offering turns to ashes, and the worship becomes fruitless. / From giving the god’s food-offering to a brahmin, [the fruit is] surely infinite.
The god, being pleased and granting a boon, departs to his own abode. / Having offered the food-offering to the god, if a fool consumes it himself,
he who steals what has been given, consuming the property of the god, goes to hell.

4.21.s:
yathā babhau śaraccandro jyotiṣāmantare ca khe ..
śrutvā tamūcuste sarve jagatāmīśvaraṃ param .. 46 ..
4.21.d:
यथा बभौ शरच्चन्द्रो ज्योतिषामन्तरे च खे ॥
श्रुत्वा तमूचुस्ते सर्वे जगतामीश्वरं परम् ॥ 46 ॥

4.21.s:
svecchāmayaṃ guṇātītaṃ jyotīrūpaṃ sanātanam ..
dṛṣṭvā mahotsavaṃ śīghramuvāca pitaraṃ hariḥ ..
sarveṣāṃ durlabhāṃ nītiṃ nītiśāstraviśāradaḥ .. 47 ..
4.21.d:
स्वेच्छामयं गुणातीतं ज्योतीरूपं सनातनम् ॥
दृष्ट्वा महोत्सवं शीघ्रमुवाच पितरं हरिः ॥
सर्वेषां दुर्लभां नीतिं नीतिशास्त्रविशारदः ॥ 47 ॥

4.21.s:
śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca ..
bhobho ballavarājeṃdra kiṃ karoṣīha suvrata .. 48 ..
4.21.d:
श्रीकृष्ण उवाच ॥
भोभो बल्लवराजेंद्र किं करोषीह सुव्रत ॥ 48 ॥

4.21.s:
ārādhyaḥ kaśca kā pūjā kiṃ phalaṃ pūjane bhavet ..
phalena sādhanaṃ kiṃ vā kaḥ sakhyaḥ sādhanena ca .. 49 ..
4.21.d:
आराध्यः कश्च का पूजा किं फलं पूजने भवेत् ॥
फलेन साधनं किं वा कः सख्यः साधनेन च ॥ 49 ॥

4.21.s:
deve ruṣṭe bhavetkiṃ vā pūjāyāḥ pratibandhake ..
tuṣṭo devaḥ kiṃ dadāti phalamatra paratrakam .. 4.21.50 ..
4.21.d:
देवे रुष्टे भवेत्किं वा पूजायाः प्रतिबन्धके ॥
तुष्टो देवः किं ददाति फलमत्र परत्रकम् ॥ 4.21.50 ॥

4.21.s:
kāciddadātyatra phalaṃ paratreha na kācana ..
kācicca nobhayatrāpi cobhayatrāpi kācana .. 51 ..
4.21.d:
काचिद्ददात्यत्र फलं परत्रेह न काचन ॥
काचिच्च नोभयत्रापि चोभयत्रापि काचन ॥ 51 ॥

4.21.s:
avedavihitā pūjā sarvahānikaraṇḍikā ..
pūjeyamadhunā vā te kimu vā puruṣakramāt .. 52 ..
4.21.d:
अवेदविहिता पूजा सर्वहानिकरण्डिका ॥
पूजेयमधुना वा ते किमु वा पुरुषक्रमात् ॥ 52 ॥

4.21.s:
dṛṣṭo devastvayā kasminpūjeyaṃ cānusāriṇī ..
sākṣātkhādati devaste sākṣātkiṃ vā na khādati .. 53 ..
4.21.d:
दृष्टो देवस्त्वया कस्मिन्पूजेयं चानुसारिणी ॥
साक्षात्खादति देवस्ते साक्षात्किं वा न खादति ॥ 53 ॥

4.21.s:
sākṣādbhuṅkte ca yo devaḥ supraśastaṃ tadarcanam ..
sākṣātkhādati naivedyaṃ viprarūpī janārdanaḥ .. 54 ..
4.21.d:
साक्षाद्भुङ्क्ते च यो देवः सुप्रशस्तं तदर्चनम् ॥
साक्षात्खादति नैवेद्यं विप्ररूपी जनार्दनः ॥ 54 ॥

4.21.s:
brāhmaṇe parituṣṭe ca saṃtuṣṭāḥ sarvadevatāḥ ..
kiṃ tasya devapūjāyāṃ yo niyukto dvijārcane .. 55 ..
4.21.d:
ब्राह्मणे परितुष्टे च संतुष्टाः सर्वदेवताः ॥
किं तस्य देवपूजायां यो नियुक्तो द्विजार्चने ॥ 55 ॥

4.21.s:
pūjitā brāhmaṇā yena pūjitāḥ sarvadevatāḥ ..
devāya dattvā naivedyaṃ dvijāya na prayacchati .. 56 ..
4.21.d:
पूजिता ब्राह्मणा येन पूजिताः सर्वदेवताः ॥
देवाय दत्त्वा नैवेद्यं द्विजाय न प्रयच्छति ॥ 56 ॥

4.21.s:
bhasmībhūtaṃ ca naivedyaṃ pūjanaṃ niṣphalaṃ bhavet..
viprāya devanaivedyadānāddhruvamanantakam ..57..
4.21.d:
भस्मीभूतं च नैवेद्यं पूजनं निष्फलं भवेत्॥
विप्राय देवनैवेद्यदानाद्ध्रुवमनन्तकम् ॥57॥

4.21.s:
tuṣṭo devo varaṃ dattvā prayāti ca svamandiram ..
dattvā devāya naivedyaṃ mūḍho bhuṅkte svayaṃ yadi..58..
4.21.d:
तुष्टो देवो वरं दत्त्वा प्रयाति च स्वमन्दिरम् ॥
दत्त्वा देवाय नैवेद्यं मूढो भुङ्क्ते स्वयं यदि॥58॥

4.21.s:
dattāpahārī devasvaṃ bhuktvā ca narakaṃ vrajet ..
devadattaṃ na bhoktavyaṃ naivedyaṃ ca vinā hareḥ ..99..
4.21.d:
दत्तापहारी देवस्वं भुक्त्वा च नरकं व्रजेत् ॥
देवदत्तं न भोक्तव्यं नैवेद्यं च विना हरेः ॥99॥

4.21.s:
praśastaṃ sarvadeveṣu viṣṇunaivedyabhojanam..
annaṃ viṣṭhā jalaṃ mūtraṃ yadviṣṇoraniveditam .. 4.21.60 ..
4.21.d:
प्रशस्तं सर्वदेवेषु विष्णुनैवेद्यभोजनम्॥
अन्नं विष्ठा जलं मूत्रं यद्विष्णोरनिवेदितम् ॥ 4.21.60 ॥

4.21.s:
sarveṣāṃ ca kramamidaṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ viśeṣataḥ ..
na dattvā vastu devāya dattaṃ viprāya cetsudhīḥ .. 61 ..
4.21.d:
सर्वेषां च क्रममिदं ब्राह्मणानां विशेषतः ॥
न दत्त्वा वस्तु देवाय दत्तं विप्राय चेत्सुधीः ॥ 61 ॥

4.21.s:
bhuktvā vipramukhe devāstuṣṭāḥ svargaṃ prayānti ca ..
tasmātsarvaprayatnena viprāṇāmarcanaṃ kuru ..62..
4.21.d:
भुक्त्वा विप्रमुखे देवास्तुष्टाः स्वर्गं प्रयान्ति च ॥
तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन विप्राणामर्चनं कुरु ॥62॥

4.21.s:
praśastaphaladātṝṇāmiha loke paratra ca..
japastapaśca pūjā vā yajñadānaṃ mahotsavam .. 63 ..
4.21.d:
प्रशस्तफलदातॄणामिह लोके परत्र च॥
जपस्तपश्च पूजा वा यज्ञदानं महोत्सवम् ॥ 63 ॥

4.21.s:
sarveṣāṃ karmaṇāṃ sāraṃ vipratuṣṭiśca dakṣiṇā ..
dakṣiṇānāṃ śarīreṣu tiṣṭhanti sarvadevatāḥ .. ..64..
4.21.d:
सर्वेषां कर्मणां सारं विप्रतुष्टिश्च दक्षिणा ॥
दक्षिणानां शरीरेषु तिष्ठन्ति सर्वदेवताः ॥ ॥64॥

4.21.s:
pādeṣu sarvatīrthāni puṇyāni pādadhūliṣu ..
pādodake ca viprāṇāṃ tīrthatoyāni santi ca .. 65 ..
4.21.d:
पादेषु सर्वतीर्थानि पुण्यानि पादधूलिषु ॥
पादोदके च विप्राणां तीर्थतोयानि सन्ति च ॥ 65 ॥

4.21.s:
tatsparśātsarvatīrtheṣu snānajanyaphalaṃ labhet ..
naśyaṃti bhakṣaṇādrogā bhaktibhāvena ballava ..66..
4.21.d:
तत्स्पर्शात्सर्वतीर्थेषु स्नानजन्यफलं लभेत् ॥
नश्यंति भक्षणाद्रोगा भक्तिभावेन बल्लव ॥66॥

4.21.s:
saptajanmakṛtātpāpānmucyante nātra saṃśayaḥ ..
pāpaṃ pañcavidhaṃ kṛtvā yo vipraṃ praṇamedvraje ..67..
4.21.d:
सप्तजन्मकृतात्पापान्मुच्यन्ते नात्र संशयः ॥
पापं पञ्चविधं कृत्वा यो विप्रं प्रणमेद्व्रजे ॥67॥

4.21.s:
sa snātaḥ sarvatīrtheṣu sarvapāpātpramucyate ..
brāhmaṇasparśamātreṇa mukto bhavati pātakī .. 68 ..
4.21.d:
स स्नातः सर्वतीर्थेषु सर्वपापात्प्रमुच्यते ॥
ब्राह्मणस्पर्शमात्रेण मुक्तो भवति पातकी ॥ 68 ॥

4.21.s:
darśanānmucyate pāpāditi vede nirūpitam ..
aprājño vā'tha prājño vā brāhmaṇo viṣṇuvigrahaḥ .. 69 ..
4.21.d:
दर्शनान्मुच्यते पापादिति वेदे निरूपितम् ॥
अप्राज्ञो वाऽथ प्राज्ञो वा ब्राह्मणो विष्णुविग्रहः ॥ 69 ॥

4.21.s:
priyāḥ prāṇādhikā viṣṇorye viprā harisevinaḥ ..
dvijānāṃ haribhaktānāṃ prabhāvo durlabhaḥ śrutau ..4.21.70..
4.21.d:
प्रियाः प्राणाधिका विष्णोर्ये विप्रा हरिसेविनः ॥
द्विजानां हरिभक्तानां प्रभावो दुर्लभः श्रुतौ ॥4.21.70॥

4.21.s:
yeṣāṃ pādābjarajasā sadyaḥ pūtā vasundharā..
teṣāṃ ca pādacihnaṃ yattīrthaṃ tatparikīrtitam .. 71 ..
4.21.d:
येषां पादाब्जरजसा सद्यः पूता वसुन्धरा॥
तेषां च पादचिह्नं यत्तीर्थं तत्परिकीर्तितम् ॥ 71 ॥

4.21.s:
teṣāṃ ca sparśamātreṇa tīrthapāpaṃ praṇaśyati ..
āliṅganātsadālāpātteṣāmucchiṣṭabhojanāt .. .. 72 ..
4.21.d:
तेषां च स्पर्शमात्रेण तीर्थपापं प्रणश्यति ॥
आलिङ्गनात्सदालापात्तेषामुच्छिष्टभोजनात् ॥ ॥ 72 ॥

4.21.s:
darśanātsparśanāccaiva sarvapāpātpramucyate ..
bhramaṇe sarvatīrthānāṃ yatpuṇyaṃ snānato bhavet ..73..
4.21.d:
दर्शनात्स्पर्शनाच्चैव सर्वपापात्प्रमुच्यते ॥
भ्रमणे सर्वतीर्थानां यत्पुण्यं स्नानतो भवेत् ॥73॥
4.21.m:
Food offering given to any deity should not be eaten, except that of Hari. / Eating Viṣṇu's food offering is praised above that of all gods. / Food unoffered to Viṣṇu is feces; water [unoffered to Viṣṇu] is urine.
This is the rule for all, and especially for brāhmaṇas. / If a wise man gives something to a brāhmaṇa without having offered it to God,
the gods, eating through the mouth of the brāhmaṇa, are satisfied and go to heaven. / Therefore, with every effort, worship brāhmaṇas
who bestow splendid fruit in this world and the next. / Recitation, asceticism, worship, sacrificial donation, or a great festival—
the essence of all rites is the satisfaction of brāhmaṇas and the priestly gift. / All the gods reside in the bodies of the priests who receive gifts.
All sacred shrines reside in their feet, and merits reside in the dust of their feet; / and in the water that washed the feet of brāhmaṇas are all the waters of sacred shrines.
From touching it, one obtains the fruit born of bathing in all sacred shrines. / From consuming it with an attitude of devotion, cowherd, diseases perish;
people are freed from sin committed over seven lifetimes, without doubt. / Having committed the five kinds of sins, whoever bows to a brāhmaṇa in Vraja
is as one who has bathed in all sacred shrines, and is freed from all sins. / Merely by touching a brāhmaṇa, a sinner becomes liberated;
by seeing [a brāhmaṇa], one is freed from sin—so it is determined in the Veda. / Whether ignorant or wise, a brāhmaṇa is the very form of Viṣṇu.
Brāhmaṇas who are devoted servants of Hari are dearer to Viṣṇu than his own breath. / The power of twice-born devotees of Hari is rarely heard of even in the Veda.
By the dust of whose lotus feet the earth is immediately sanctified, / the footprint of these is proclaimed to be a sacred shrine.
And by merely touching them, sins incurred at sacred shrines perish; / from embracing, constantly conversing, and eating their leftovers,
from seeing and touching [them], one is completely freed from all sins. / Whatever merit comes from wandering to all sacred shrines and bathing [in them],

4.21.s:
haridāsasya viprasya tatpuṇyaṃ darśanāllabhet ..
ye viprā haraye dattvā nityamannaṃ ca bhuñjate ..74..
4.21.d:
हरिदासस्य विप्रस्य तत्पुण्यं दर्शनाल्लभेत् ॥
ये विप्रा हरये दत्त्वा नित्यमन्नं च भुञ्जते ॥74॥
4.21.m:
one obtains that merit simply by seeing a brāhmaṇa servant of Hari. / Those brāhmaṇas who eat food only after offering it daily to Hari—
from eating their leftovers, a man obtains the status of a servant of Hari. / If, even through error, people eat without offering with devotion to Hari,
the substance becomes like feces, and water becomes equal to urine. / If a śūdra is a devotee of Hari and eager to eat the food offering,
he offers uncooked grain to Hari, cooks it, and eats it. / Brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, and vaiśyas have the right to worship the Śālagrāma stone;
śūdras have no right to do so, nor likewise to worship Hari directly. / If you do not give these items to the brāhmaṇas, O king of cowherds,
they will all turn to ashes, without doubt. / And one ought to give food to all living beings for the sake of merit.
By giving to superior beings, one obtains superior fruit. / Hence, by giving to human beings, one obtains eight times the fruit.
Giving food to vaiśyas brings twice the merit of giving to śūdras; / giving food to kṣatriyas brings twice that of vaiśyas;
giving food to brāhmaṇas brings a hundred times that of kṣatriyas. / The fruit given to a brāhmaṇa learned in the scriptures is a hundred times that of ordinary brāhmaṇas;
one certainly obtains a hundred times the fruit of those learned in the scriptures in a brāhmaṇa who is a devotee.
And he offers that food to Hari and eats it with devotion and reverence. / Whatever fruit belongs to a donor who gives to Viṣṇu, who is devoted to brāhmaṇas,
one truly obtains that fruit by feeding a brāhmaṇa devotee. / When the devotee is pleased, Hari is pleased; and when Hari is pleased, the gods
become fully satisfied, just as the branches [flourish] from watering the root. / If you offer these items to just one deity,
and all the [other] gods are displeased, what will anyone do against the gods? / Or else give half of the goods to Govardhana.

4.21.s:
ucchiṣṭabhojanātteṣāṃ harerdāsyaṃ labhennaraḥ ..
na dattvā haraye bhaktyā bhuñjate cedbhramādapi .. 75 ..
4.21.d:
उच्छिष्टभोजनात्तेषां हरेर्दास्यं लभेन्नरः ॥
न दत्त्वा हरये भक्त्या भुञ्जते चेद्भ्रमादपि ॥ 75 ॥

4.21.s:
purīṣasadṛśaṃ vastu jalaṃ mūtrasamaṃ bhavet ..
śūdraśceddharibhaktaśca naivedyabhojanotsukaḥ .. 76 .. (tu. brahmavaivarta 2.10.49)
4.21.d:
पुरीषसदृशं वस्तु जलं मूत्रसमं भवेत् ॥
शूद्रश्चेद्धरिभक्तश्च नैवेद्यभोजनोत्सुकः ॥ 76 ॥ (तु। ब्रह्मवैवर्त 2.10.49)

4.21.s:
āmānnaṃ haraye dattvā kṛtvā pākaṃ ca khādati ..
viprakṣatriyavaiśyānāṃ śālagrāmaśilārcane ..77..
4.21.d:
आमान्नं हरये दत्त्वा कृत्वा पाकं च खादति ॥
विप्रक्षत्रियवैश्यानां शालग्रामशिलार्चने ॥77॥

4.21.s:
adhikāro na śūdrāṇāṃ harerapyarcane tathā ..
dravyāṇyetāni gopendra viprebhyaścenna dāsyati ..78..
4.21.d:
अधिकारो न शूद्राणां हरेरप्यर्चने तथा ॥
द्रव्याण्येतानि गोपेन्द्र विप्रेभ्यश्चेन्न दास्यति ॥78॥

4.21.s:
bhasmībhūtāni sarvāṇi bhaviṣyanti na saṃśayaḥ ..
annaṃ ca sarvajīvebhyaḥ puṇyārthaṃ dātumarhati .. 79 ..
4.21.d:
भस्मीभूतानि सर्वाणि भविष्यन्ति न संशयः ॥
अन्नं च सर्वजीवेभ्यः पुण्यार्थं दातुमर्हति ॥ 79 ॥

4.21.s:
dattvā viśiṣṭajīvebhyo viśiṣṭaṃ phalamāpnuyāt ..
ato dattvā mānuṣebhyo labhate'ṣṭaguṇaṃ phalam .. 4.21.80 ..
4.21.d:
दत्त्वा विशिष्टजीवेभ्यो विशिष्टं फलमाप्नुयात् ॥
अतो दत्त्वा मानुषेभ्यो लभतेऽष्टगुणं फलम् ॥ 4.21.80 ॥

4.21.s:
śūdrāṇāṃ dviguṇaṃ puṇyaṃ vaiśyebhyo'nnaṃ pradāya ca..
dattvā'nnaṃ kṣatriyebhyo'pi vaiśyānāṃ dviguṇaṃ bhavet..
kṣattriyāṇāṃ śataguṇaṃ viprebhyo'nnaṃ pradāya ca .. 81 ..
4.21.d:
शूद्राणां द्विगुणं पुण्यं वैश्येभ्योऽन्नं प्रदाय च॥
दत्त्वाऽन्नं क्षत्रियेभ्योऽपि वैश्यानां द्विगुणं भवेत्॥
क्षत्त्रियाणां शतगुणं विप्रेभ्योऽन्नं प्रदाय च ॥ 81 ॥

4.21.s:
viprāṇāṃ ca śataguṇaṃ śāstrajñe brāhmaṇe phalam ..
śāstrajñānāṃ śataguṇaṃ bhakte vipre labheddhruvam .. 82 ..
4.21.d:
विप्राणां च शतगुणं शास्त्रज्ञे ब्राह्मणे फलम् ॥
शास्त्रज्ञानां शतगुणं भक्ते विप्रे लभेद्ध्रुवम् ॥ 82 ॥

4.21.s:
sa cānnaṃ haraye dattvā bhuṅkte bhaktyā ca sādaram ..
viṣṇave viprabhaktāya dattvā dātuśca yatphalam .. 83 ..
4.21.d:
स चान्नं हरये दत्त्वा भुङ्क्ते भक्त्या च सादरम् ॥
विष्णवे विप्रभक्ताय दत्त्वा दातुश्च यत्फलम् ॥ 83 ॥

4.21.s:
tatphalaṃ labhate nūnaṃ bhaktabrāhmaṇabhojane ..
bhakte tuṣṭe haristuṣṭo harau tuṣṭe ca devatāḥ .. 84 ..
4.21.d:
तत्फलं लभते नूनं भक्तब्राह्मणभोजने ॥
भक्ते तुष्टे हरिस्तुष्टो हरौ तुष्टे च देवताः ॥ 84 ॥

4.21.s:
bhavanti siddhāḥ śākhāśca yathā mūlaniṣecanāt ..
dravyāṇyetāni devāya yadyekasmai prayacchati .. 85 ..
4.21.d:
भवन्ति सिद्धाः शाखाश्च यथा मूलनिषेचनात् ॥
द्रव्याण्येतानि देवाय यद्येकस्मै प्रयच्छति ॥ 85 ॥

4.21.s:
sarve devāśca ruṣṭāśceddevaiḥ kaḥ kiṃ kariṣyati ..
athavā'rddhaṃ ca vastūnāṃ dehi govardhanāya ca .. 86 ..
4.21.d:
सर्वे देवाश्च रुष्टाश्चेद्देवैः कः किं करिष्यति ॥
अथवाऽर्द्धं च वस्तूनां देहि गोवर्धनाय च ॥ 86 ॥

4.21.s:
gā vardhayati nityaṃ yastena govardhanaḥ smṛtaḥ ..
govardhanasamastāta puṇyavānna mahītale .. 87 ..
4.21.d:
गा वर्धयति नित्यं यस्तेन गोवर्धनः स्मृतः ॥
गोवर्धनसमस्तात पुण्यवान्न महीतले ॥ 87 ॥
4.21.m:
Because it always nurtures the cows, it is remembered as 'Govardhana'. / Father, there is no one on the surface of the earth as meritorious as Govardhana.
Whoever daily gives fresh grass to cows— / whatever merit is at sacred shrines, whatever merit is in feeding brāhmaṇas,
in all vows and fasts, and in all austerities, / whatever merit is in great giving, whatever merit is in serving Hari,
whatever comes from wandering the earth, whatever is found in all [truthful] words, / whatever merit a man obtains in all sacrifices and at initiation—
a wise person obtains all that merit simply by giving grass to cows. / Whoever willfully stops a cow that is eating grass
incurs [the sin of] murdering a brāhmaṇa, and is purified [only] through expiation. / All the gods are in the cow's body, and the sacred shrines are in her feet;
Lakṣmī herself always resides in her secret parts, O father. / Indeed, that man who makes a sectarian mark with mud touched by a cow’s hoof
immediately becomes as one who has bathed in sacred shrines, and victory is his at every step. / Wherever cows stand, that very place is proclaimed a sacred shrine;
a man abandoning his life there certainly becomes liberated at once. / That vile man who strikes the body of brāhmaṇas or cows
incurs a sin equal to murdering a brāhmaṇa, without doubt. / Those men who kill cows and brāhmaṇas, who are portions of Nārāyaṇa,
go to Kālasūtra for as long as the moon and sun endure." / Having spoken thus, Śrī Kṛṣṇa paused, O Nārada.
And Nanda, filled with joy, spoke to him with a smiling face. / Nanda said: / "This worship of the great Mahendra is traditional;
it causes good rain, and brings about all delightful crops. / Crops are the life of living beings; living creatures live because of crops.
The people of Vraja worship Mahendra from generation to generation / with a great festival at the end of the year for the sake of freedom from obstacles and good fortune." / Having heard this speech, Mādhava, along with Bala,

4.21.s:
nityaṃ dadāti gobhyo yo navīnāni tṛṇāni ca ..
tīrthasthāneṣu yatpuṇyaṃ yatpuṇyaṃ viprabhojane .. 88 ..
4.21.d:
नित्यं ददाति गोभ्यो यो नवीनानि तृणानि च ॥
तीर्थस्थानेषु यत्पुण्यं यत्पुण्यं विप्रभोजने ॥ 88 ॥

4.21.s:
sarvavratopavāseṣu sarveṣveva tapaḥsu ca ..
yatpuṇyaṃ ca mahādāne yatpuṇyaṃ harisevane .. 89 ..
4.21.d:
सर्वव्रतोपवासेषु सर्वेष्वेव तपःसु च ॥
यत्पुण्यं च महादाने यत्पुण्यं हरिसेवने ॥ 89 ॥

4.21.s:
bhuvaḥ paryaṭane yattu sarvavākyeṣu yadbhavet ..
yatpuṇyaṃ sarvayajñeṣu dīkṣāyāṃ ca labhennaraḥ .. 4.21.90 ..
4.21.d:
भुवः पर्यटने यत्तु सर्ववाक्येषु यद्भवेत् ॥
यत्पुण्यं सर्वयज्ञेषु दीक्षायां च लभेन्नरः ॥ 4.21.90 ॥

4.21.s:
tatpuṇyaṃ labhate prājño gobhyo dattvā tṛṇāni ca ..
bhuktavantīṃ tṛṇaṃ yaśca gāṃ vārayati kāmataḥ .. 91 ..
4.21.d:
तत्पुण्यं लभते प्राज्ञो गोभ्यो दत्त्वा तृणानि च ॥
भुक्तवन्तीं तृणं यश्च गां वारयति कामतः ॥ 91 ॥

4.21.s:
brahmahatyā bhavettasya prāyaścittādviśudhyati..
sarve devā gavā maṅge tīrthāni tatpadeṣu ca .. 92 ..
4.21.d:
ब्रह्महत्या भवेत्तस्य प्रायश्चित्ताद्विशुध्यति॥
सर्वे देवा गवा मङ्गे तीर्थानि तत्पदेषु च ॥ 92 ॥

4.21.s:
tadguhyeṣu svayaṃ lakṣmīstiṣṭhatyeva sadā pitaḥ ..
goṣpadāktamṛdā yo hi tilakaṃ kurute naraḥ..93..
4.21.d:
तद्गुह्येषु स्वयं लक्ष्मीस्तिष्ठत्येव सदा पितः ॥
गोष्पदाक्तमृदा यो हि तिलकं कुरुते नरः॥93॥

4.21.s:
tīrthasnāto bhavetsadyo jayastasya padepade ..
gāvastiṣṭhaṃti yatraiva tattīrthaṃ parikīrtitam .. 94 ..
4.21.d:
तीर्थस्नातो भवेत्सद्यो जयस्तस्य पदेपदे ॥
गावस्तिष्ठंति यत्रैव तत्तीर्थं परिकीर्तितम् ॥ 94 ॥

4.21.s:
prāṇāṃstyaktā narastatra sadyo mukto bhaveddhruvam ..
brāhmaṇānāṃ gavāmaṅgaṃ yo hanti mānavādhamaḥ .. 95 ..
4.21.d:
प्राणांस्त्यक्ता नरस्तत्र सद्यो मुक्तो भवेद्ध्रुवम् ॥
ब्राह्मणानां गवामङ्गं यो हन्ति मानवाधमः ॥ 95 ॥

4.21.s:
brahmahatyāsamaṃ pāpaṃ bhavettasya na saṃśayaḥ ..
nārāyaṇāṃśānviprāṃśca gāśca ye ghnanti mānavāḥ .. 96 ..
4.21.d:
ब्रह्महत्यासमं पापं भवेत्तस्य न संशयः ॥
नारायणांशान्विप्रांश्च गाश्च ये घ्नन्ति मानवाः ॥ 96 ॥

4.21.s:
kālasūtraṃ ca te yānti yāvaccandradivākarau ..
ityevamuktvā śrīkṛṣṇo virarāma ca nārada ..97..
4.21.d:
कालसूत्रं च ते यान्ति यावच्चन्द्रदिवाकरौ ॥
इत्येवमुक्त्वा श्रीकृष्णो विरराम च नारद ॥97॥

4.21.s:
ānandayukto nandaśca tamuvāca smitānanaḥ ..
nanda uvāca ..
paurvāparīyaṃ pūjeti mahendrasya mahātmanaḥ .. 98 ..
4.21.d:
आनन्दयुक्तो नन्दश्च तमुवाच स्मिताननः ॥
नन्द उवाच ॥
पौर्वापरीयं पूजेति महेन्द्रस्य महात्मनः ॥ 98 ॥

4.21.s:
suvṛṣṭisādhanī sādhyaṃ sarvasasyamanoharam ..
sasyāni prāṇināṃ prāṇāḥ sasyājjīvanti jīvinaḥ..99..
4.21.d:
सुवृष्टिसाधनी साध्यं सर्वसस्यमनोहरम् ॥
सस्यानि प्राणिनां प्राणाः सस्याज्जीवन्ति जीविनः॥99॥

4.21.s:
pūjayanti vrajasthāśca mahendraṃ puruṣakramāt..
mahotsavaṃ vatsarānte nirvighnāya śivāya ca .. 4.21.100 ..
ityevaṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā balena saha mādhavaḥ ..
uccairjahāsa sa punaruvāca pitaraṃ mudā .. 4.21.1 ..
śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca ..
aho śrutaṃ vicitraṃ te vacanaṃ paramādbhutam ..
upahāsyaṃ lokaśāstraṃ vedeṣveva vigarhitam .. 2..
nirūpaṇaṃ nāsti kutra śakrādvṛṣṭiḥ prajāyate ..
apūrvaṃ nītivacanaṃ śrutamadya mukhāttava .. 3 ..
śruṇu nītiṃ śrutimatāṃ he tāta nānayaṃ vadeḥ ..
vacanaṃ sāmavedoktaṃ santo jānanti sarvata..4..
praśnaṃ kuruṣva mantrāṃśca vividhānapi saṃsadi..
bruvantu paramārthaṃ ca kimindrādvṛṣṭireva ca..5..

tebhyo'nnāni phalānyeva tebhyo jīvanti jīvinaḥ ..6..
4.21.d:
पूजयन्ति व्रजस्थाश्च महेन्द्रं पुरुषक्रमात्॥
महोत्सवं वत्सरान्ते निर्विघ्नाय शिवाय च ॥ 4.21.100 ॥
इत्येवं वचनं श्रुत्वा बलेन सह माधवः ॥
उच्चैर्जहास स पुनरुवाच पितरं मुदा ॥ 4.21.1 ॥
श्रीकृष्ण उवाच ॥
अहो श्रुतं विचित्रं ते वचनं परमाद्भुतम् ॥
उपहास्यं लोकशास्त्रं वेदेष्वेव विगर्हितम् ॥ 2॥
निरूपणं नास्ति कुत्र शक्राद्वृष्टिः प्रजायते ॥
अपूर्वं नीतिवचनं श्रुतमद्य मुखात्तव ॥ 3 ॥
श्रुणु नीतिं श्रुतिमतां हे तात नानयं वदेः ॥
वचनं सामवेदोक्तं सन्तो जानन्ति सर्वत॥4॥
प्रश्नं कुरुष्व मन्त्रांश्च विविधानपि संसदि॥
ब्रुवन्तु परमार्थं च किमिन्द्राद्वृष्टिरेव च॥5॥
सूर्याद्धि जायते तोयं तोयात्सस्यानि शाखिनः ॥
तेभ्योऽन्नानि फलान्येव तेभ्यो जीवन्ति जीविनः ॥6॥

4.21.s:
sūryagrastaṃ ca nīraṃ ca kāle tasmātsamudbhavaḥ..

sasyādhipo nṛpo mantrī vidhātrā te nirūpitāḥ ..8..
jalādikānāṃ sasyānāṃ tṛṇānāṃ ca nirūpitam ..
abde'bde'styeva tatsarvaṃ kalpe kalpe yugeyuge .. 9 ..
4.21.d:
सूर्यग्रस्तं च नीरं च काले तस्मात्समुद्भवः॥
सूर्यो मेघादयः सर्वे विधात्रा ते निरूपिताः ॥ 7 ॥
यत्राब्दे यो जलधरो गजश्च सागरो मतः ॥
सस्याधिपो नृपो मन्त्री विधात्रा ते निरूपिताः ॥8॥
जलादिकानां सस्यानां तृणानां च निरूपितम् ॥
अब्देऽब्देऽस्त्येव तत्सर्वं कल्पे कल्पे युगेयुगे ॥ 9 ॥

4.21.s:
hastī samudrādādāya kareṇa jalamīpsitam ..
dadyādghanāya taddadyādvātena prerito ghanaḥ .. 4.21.110 ..
sthānesthāne pṛthivyāṃ ca kālekāle yathocitam..
īśecchayā''virbhūtaṃ ca na bhavetpratibandhakam .. 11 ..

jagaccarācaraṃ sarvaṃ kṛtaṃ teneśvarājñayā ..
ādau vinirmitaṃ bhakṣyaṃ paścājjīva iti smṛtaḥ .. 13 ..

4.21.d:
हस्ती समुद्रादादाय करेण जलमीप्सितम् ॥
दद्याद्घनाय तद्दद्याद्वातेन प्रेरितो घनः ॥ 4.21.110 ॥
स्थानेस्थाने पृथिव्यां च कालेकाले यथोचितम्॥
ईशेच्छया'ऽविर्भूतं च न भवेत्प्रतिबन्धकम् ॥ 11 ॥
भूतं भव्यं भविष्यच्च महत्क्षुद्रं च मध्यमम् ॥
धात्रा निरूपितं कर्म केन तात निवार्यते ॥ 12॥
जगच्चराचरं सर्वं कृतं तेनेश्वराज्ञया ॥
आदौ विनिर्मितं भक्ष्यं पश्चाज्जीव इति स्मृतः ॥ 13 ॥
अभ्यासात्स स्वभावो हि स्वभावात्कर्म एव च ॥
जायते कर्मणां भोगो जीविनां सुखदुःखयोः ॥ 14 ॥
यातनाजन्ममरणरोगशोकभयानि च ॥
समुत्पत्तिर्विपद्विद्या कविता वा यशोऽयशः ॥ 15 ॥
पुण्यं च स्वर्गवासश्च पापं नरकसंस्थितिः ॥
भुक्तिर्मुक्तिर्हरेर्दास्यं कर्मणा घटते नृणाम् ॥ 16 ॥
4.21.m:
He laughed loudly and spoke again to his father with joy.
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
“Ah, I have heard your extraordinary, most wonderful words!
They are laughable to ordinary lore and condemned in the Vedas themselves.
Nowhere is it determined that rain arises from Śakra.
Today an unprecedented moral teaching has been heard from your mouth!
Listen to the morality of those versed in the Vedas, O father; do not speak unrighteousness!
The virtuous everywhere know the teaching spoken in the Sāmaveda.
Ask questions and examine the various mantras in the assembly!
Let them state the absolute truth: does rain indeed come from Indra?
For from the sun arises water; from water come the crops and trees;
from them come food and fruits; from them living beings live.
Water is absorbed by the sun, and from it rain comes forth in due time.
The sun, clouds, and all else are assigned by the Creator.
Which cloud, which elephant, and which ocean belongs to which year,
and the ruler of crops, the king, and the minister—all are appointed by the Creator.
The assignment of water and the like, of crops, and of grasses
exists year after year, kalpa after kalpa, yuga after yuga.
The elephant, taking the desired water from the ocean with its trunk,
gives it to the cloud; driven by the wind, the cloud pours it down
in place after place upon the earth, and at the proper time in every season.
What has manifested by the Lord's will can have no hindrance.
Past, present, and future, the great, the small, and the middling—
who can avert the action determined by the Creator, O father?
The entire universe of moving and unmoving things was made by the Lord's command;
first food was fashioned, and afterwards, it is taught, the living creature.
From habit comes one's nature, and from nature indeed arises action;
from their actions arises the experiencing of pleasure and pain for living beings.
Torments, birth, death, disease, grief, and fear,
origin, calamity, learning or poetry, fame and infamy,
merit, dwelling in heaven, sin, and staying in hell,
enjoyment, liberation, and servitude to Hari occur for men through action.
For the Lord is the father of all, as well as the practice of virtuous deeds;
he is the dispenser of fruits to the creator, and everything happens by his will.
He by whom the Virāj, the elements, Prakṛti, the universe,
the tortoise, Śeṣa, the earth, and everything from Brahmā down to a clump of grass were fashioned—
by whose command the wind supports the tortoise, and he bears Śeṣa,
Śeṣa supports the earth with his head, and she supports all moving and unmoving things;
by whose command the breath of the world blows always in the three worlds,
and the sun, maker of bright light, burns as it circles the terrestrial globe;
fire burns, and death moves among all creatures;
the generation of trees, their flowers and their fruits occurs at the right time;
and oceans quickly subside downwards into their own places now—
worship that Lord with devotion! What can Śakra do?
How many kinds of cosmic eggs have appeared and vanished,
and how many kinds of creators, by the mere play of his knit brow?
He is the death of death, the time of Time, and the creator of the Creator.
Seek refuge in him, father; he will protect you.
Ah, when twenty-eight Indras fall in a single day and night
of the Creator of the worlds, whose lifespan exceeds one hundred and eight years,
and his fall occurs in a mere twinkling of an eye of that Lord, the Nirguṇa Self—
while such a Lord exists, worship of Śakra is a mockery!”
Having spoken thus, Śrī Kṛṣṇa fell silent, O Nārada;
and the sages and the members of the assembly praised the Lord.
Nanda, thrilled with horripilation, rejoiced in the assembly with tearful eyes;
for men are filled with joy when defeated by their sons.
Recognising the instruction of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, he performed the recitation of auspicious blessings;
he then duly carried out the formal worship of all.
He then performed the worship of the mountain, of the lordly sages,

4.21.m:
of the wise, of the brāhmaṇas, of the cows, and of fire with reverence.
Then, at the completion of the worship and at the sacrificial grand festival,
there arose a mighty sound of various musical instruments.
There arose cries of victory, the blast of conches, and cries of “Hari!”;
and the foremost of sages recited the auspicious sections of the Veda.
Ḍiṇḍin, the foremost of bards and dear minister of Kaṃsa,
loudly recited before them the auspicious eight-verse hymn.
Kṛṣṇa went near the mountain, assumed a separate form,
and said: “I am the mountain; I eat the offerings; choose a boon!”
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said to Nanda: “Father, look at the mountain before you!
Request a boon, and good fortune shall be yours.”
The cowherd chose as his boon servitude to Hari and devotion to Hari.
Having eaten the offerings and granted the boon, [the mountain-form] vanished.
Having fed the lordly sages and the brāhmaṇas, the cowherd
gave wealth to the bards, to the brāhmaṇas, and to the sages.
Having given gifts to the sages and also to the brāhmaṇas, Nanda, filled with joy,
went to his own abode with his attendants, placing Rāma and Kṛṣṇa at the head.
He gave silver, clothing, gold, an excellent horse, gems,
and various kinds of edible goods to the bard Ḍiṇḍin.
Having praised and bowed to Rāma and Kṛṣṇa, the sages and brāhmaṇas departed;
all the apsarases, gandharvas, and kinnaras also departed.
All the kings and cowherds who had been invited to the great festival
bowed to Śrī Kṛṣṇa and departed with reverence.
In the meantime Śakra, his lip trembling with rage,
having heard of the disruption of the sacrifice and many kinds of censures, the lord of the gods,
mounting his chariot in haste along with the Maruts and the rain-clouds,
went to Nanda’s settlement, the enchanting forest of Vṛndāvana.
All the gods followed after him, skilled in the science of warfare.

4.21.m:
With weapons and missiles in hand, mounting his chariot in anger, O Nārada, / with sounds of wind, sounds of clouds, and terrifying sounds of the army, / the entire settlement trembled, and Nanda was seized with terror.
Addressing his wife and his people, afflicted with grief,
and leading them to a secluded place, he who was skilled in the science of conduct [spoke].

4.21.m:
“O Yaśodā, come here! Listen to my words, O Rohiṇī!
Taking Rāma and Kṛṣṇa, go far away from Vraja, dear wife!
Let the boys, girls, and women, overcome with fear, go far away.
Let the strong cowherds stay near me,
and afterwards we too shall escape from this peril to our lives.”
he praised the husband of Śacī with a hymn from the Kāṇva recension.
Having spoken thus, the foremost of cowherds remembered Śrī Hari in fear.

दिवस्पतिः शतमखः सुत्रामा गोत्रभिद्विभुः ॥

संक्रन्दनो दुश्च्यवनस्तुराषाण्मेघवाहनः ॥
आखण्डलो हरिहयो नमुचिप्राणनाशनः ॥ 55 ॥
वृद्धश्रवा वृषश्चैव दैत्यदर्पनिषूदनः ॥
षट्चत्वारिंशन्नामानि पापघ्नानि विनिश्चितम् ॥ 56 ॥
स्तोत्रमेतत्कौथुमोक्तं नित्यं यदि पठेन्नरः ॥
महाविपत्तौ शक्रस्तं वज्रहस्तश्च रक्षति ॥ 57 ॥
4.21.m:
“Indra, Lord of the gods, Śakra, son of Diti [in adoptive sense], elder brother of Pavana,
the thousand-eyed, whose body has marks [of the yoni], son of Kaśyapa,
Biḍaujas, Sunāsīra, Marutvān, Pākaśāsana,
father of Jayanta, the glorious, Lord of Śacī, slayer of Daityas,
holding the thunderbolt in hand, friend of Kāma, destroyer of Gautamī’s vow,
slayer of Vṛtra, Vāsava, beggar of Dadhīci’s body,
Viṣṇu, brother of Vāmana, Puruhūta, Purandara,
Lord of the sky, Śatamakha, Sutrāman, Gotrabhid, the all-pervading,
foremost of gods, enemy of Bala, slayer of Jambha, refuge of the gods,
Saṃkrandana, Duścyavana, Turāṣāh, whose vehicle is the cloud,
Ākhaṇḍala, whose horses are tawny, destroyer of the life of Namuci,
Vṛddhaśravas, Vṛṣan, and crusher of the pride of Daityas—
these forty-six names surely destroy sin.
If a man constantly recites this hymn declared in the Kauthuma recension,
Śakra, bearing the thunderbolt in his hand, protects him in great danger.

अतिवृष्टिशिलावृष्टिवज्रपाताच्च दारुणात् ॥
कदाचिन्न भयं तस्य रक्षिता वासवः स्वयम् ॥ 58 ॥
यत्र गेहे स्तोत्रमिदं यश्च जानाति पुण्यवान् ॥
न तत्र वज्रपतनं शिलावृष्टिश्च नारद ॥ 59 ॥
श्रीनारायण उवाच ॥
स्तोत्रं नंदमुखाच्छ्रुत्वा चुकोप मधुसूदनः ॥4.21.60॥
उवाच पितरं नीतिं प्रज्वलन्ब्रह्मतेजसा ॥
कं स्तौषि भीरो को वेन्द्रस्त्यज भीतिं ममान्तिके ॥ 61 ॥
क्षणार्द्धे भस्मसात्कर्तुं क्षमोऽहमवलीलया॥
गाश्च वत्सांश्च बालांश्च योषितो हि भयातुराः ॥62॥
गोवर्धनस्य कुहरे संस्थाप्य तिष्ठ निर्भयम् ॥
बालस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा तच्चकार मुदाऽन्वितः ॥ 63 ॥
हरिर्दधार शैलं तं वामहस्तेन दण्डवत् ॥
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे तत्र दीप्तोऽपि रत्नतेजसा ॥ 64 ॥
अन्धीभूतश्च सहसा बभूव रजसा'ऽवृतः ॥
सवातो मेघनिकरश्चच्छाद गगनं मुने ॥ 65 ॥
4.21.m:
From torrential rain, hail, and the terrible fall of thunderbolts,
he has no fear at any time; Vāsava himself is his protector.
In whichever house this hymn is present, and whichever virtuous person knows it,
no thunderbolt strikes there, nor does hailstorm fall, O Nārada.”
Hearing the hymn from Nanda's mouth, Madhusūdana became angry.
Blazing with the splendour of Brahman, he spoke words of wisdom to his father:
“Whom do you praise, timid one? Who is Indra? Cast aside fear in my presence!
In half a moment, I am able to reduce [him] to ashes with effortless ease.
Placing the cows, calves, boys, and women who are stricken with fear
in the cavity of Govardhana, remain without fear!”
Hearing the child's words, filled with joy, he did just that.
Hari held up that mountain with his left hand like a staff.
In the meantime there, though glowing with the brilliance of jewels,
everything suddenly became blinded, enveloped in dust.
A mass of clouds accompanied by wind covered the sky, O sage.

वृन्दावने बभूवातिवृष्टिरेव निरन्तरम्॥
शिलावृष्टिर्वज्रवृष्टिरुल्कापातः सुदारुणः ॥ 66 ॥

4.21.m:
In Vṛndāvana, torrential rain poured down incessantly,
with a shower of stones, a shower of thunderbolts, and the terrible fall of meteors.
Everything, upon touching the mountain, fell far away from it.
His undertaking was rendered fruitless, like the effort of a powerless man, O sage.
Seeing all that become in vain, Śakra immediately grew enraged.
He seized the unfailing thunderbolt fashioned from the bones of Dadhīci.
Seeing him with the thunderbolt in his hand, Madhusūdana laughed.
He paralysed the terrible thunderbolt along with the hand [that held it].

4.21.m:
The Lord rendered him and the host of immortals completely paralysed and ineffective;
they all stood motionless, like painted figures on a wall.
Made to yawn by Hari, Śakra immediately fell into drowsiness.
In that drowsiness, he beheld the entire world pervaded by Kṛṣṇa:
two-armed, flute in hand, adorned with jewelled ornaments,
clad in yellow garments, seated on a throne of gems, / his face bright with a gentle smile, eager to show grace to his devotees,
all his limbs anointed with sandalwood paste—[he saw] this entire moving and unmoving universe [as him].
Beholding this most wondrous sight there, he immediately swooned away.
Right there he muttered the mantra previously bestowed by his guru.
He beheld a dazzling light situated in a thousand-petalled lotus,
and within it a divine form, exceedingly captivating to the mind,
surpassing a fresh raincloud, a dark-and-beautiful form,
with radiant makara-shaped earrings fashioned from the essence of fine gems,

विनोदमुरलीशब्दं कुर्वन्तं कुत्रचिन्मुदा ॥ 94 ॥
गायन्तं रम्यसङ्गीतं कुत्रचिद्बालकैः सह॥
स्तुत्वा शक्रः स्तवेन्द्रेण प्रणनाम हरिं भिया ॥95॥
पुरा दत्तेन गुरुणा रणे वृत्रासुरेण च॥
कृष्णेन दत्तं कृपया ब्रह्मणे च तपस्यते ॥96॥
4.21.m:
going with Rādhā to the circle of the rāsa-dance in some place,
and wearing around his neck the garland given by Rādhā in some place; // 190
sporting with the cowherd women in some place,
taking Rādhā and going, yet abandoning her in some place; // 91
eating the food given by the wives of the brāhmaṇas in some place,
eating palmyra palm fruit with the boys in some place; // 92
joyfully stealing the clothes of the cowherd women in some place,
calling the herd of cows with the boys in some place; // 93
placing his lotus foot upon the head of Kāliya in some place,
producing the playful sound of the flute with joy in some place,
and singing pleasant songs with the boys in some place.” // 94 //
Having praised Hari with this king of hymns, Śakra bowed down out of fear. // 95
[This hymn had been] given previously in the battle with the demon Vṛtra by the guru;
it was given mercifully by Kṛṣṇa to Brahmā who was performing austerities. // 96

एकादशाक्षरो मन्त्रः कवचं सर्वलक्षणम् ॥
दत्तमेतत्कुमाराय पुष्करे ब्रह्मणा पुरा ॥97॥
कुमारोऽङ्गिरसे दत्तं गुरवेऽङ्गिरसा मुने ॥
इदमिन्द्रकृतं स्तोत्रं नित्यं भक्त्या च यः पठेत् ॥ 98 ॥

4.21.m:
The eleven-syllabled mantra and the armour having all characteristics
were given previously by Brahmā to Kumāra at Puṣkara, O sage; // 97
Kumāra gave it to Aṅgiras, and by Aṅgiras it was given to the guru [Bṛhaspati].
Whoever recites this hymn composed by Indra daily with devotion, // 98
having attained steadfast devotion, certainly obtains servitude [to the Lord] in the end.
That person is released from birth, death, old age, disease, and sorrow;
he does not see, even in a dream, Yama's messenger or Yama's abode. // 99

इन्द्रस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा प्रसन्नः श्रीनिकेतनः॥4.21.200॥

पुलकाञ्चितसर्वाङ्गो भक्तिपूर्णाश्रुलोचनः ॥ 3 ॥
नन्द उवाच ॥
नमो ब्रह्मण्यदेवाय गोब्राह्मणहिताय च ॥4॥
जगद्धिताय कृष्णाय गोविन्दाय नमोनमः ॥

निर्लिप्ताय निर्गुणाय निराकाराय ते नमः॥
अतिसूक्ष्मस्वरूपाय स्थूलात्स्थूलतमाय च ॥7॥
4.21.m:
Hearing Indra's words, the abode of Śrī was pleased. // 200
Having affectionately granted him a boon, he set down the mountain.
Bowing to Hari, Śakra departed along with his retinue. // 1
All the people inside the cave went from the cave to their homes;
they all considered Kṛṣṇa to be the most complete, all-pervading Lord. // 2
Placing the residents of Vraja at the forefront, Hari departed to his own abode.
Nanda praised his son, the complete eternal Brahman,
his whole body bristling with horripilation, his eyes full of tears of devotion.
Homage to the god devoted to Brahman, and beneficent to cows and brāhmaṇas!
Homage, homage to Kṛṣṇa, to Govinda, who brings welfare to the universe!
Homage to the god devoted to Brahman, to Brahman, the Paramātman!
Homage to you, the supreme abode of an endless crore of cosmic eggs!
Homage to the witness manifested as living beings, who took the forms of the Fish and the others!
Homage to you who are untouched [by matter], devoid of gunas, formless!
To the one whose true nature is most subtle, and grosser than the grossest,

4.21.m:
endowed with the names and qualities of white, red, yellow, and dark,
the yogin, the embodiment of yoga, the guru even of yogins,
to the lord of the perfected ones, the perfected one, the guru of the perfected ones, homage!
Whom Brahmā is unable to praise, whom Viṣṇu is unable to praise,
whom Rudra is unable to praise, whom Śeṣa is unable to praise,
whom Dharma is unable to praise, whom the Sun is unable to praise,
whom Lambodara and also the six-faced one are unable to praise,
whom all the sages, Sanaka and the rest, are unable to praise,
whom Kapila, guru of the guru of the lords among the perfected ones, cannot praise,
whom the two ṛṣis Nara and Nārāyaṇa are not able to praise,
who else of dull intellect can be able to praise the one higher than the highest?
The Vedas are not able, nor speech, nor Lakṣmī, nor Sarasvatī,
Rādhā is not able to praise—how could the wise praise [you]?
Forgive every offence, O Brahman, at every moment!

Protect me, O ocean of compassion, friend of the poor, in the ocean of worldly existence!
Having performed austerities long ago at a holy place, the eternal son was obtained.
Grant me devotion and servitude at your lotus feet!
The state of Brahmā, immortality, or even residence in the same world [as the deity] and the like—
these are not worth a sixteenth part of servitude at your lotus feet.

4.21.m:
kingship, long life—do the wise value these at all?
All this that has been mentioned, the state of Brahmā and the rest, O Lord,
how could it ever be equal to half a moment of fellowship with your devotees?
He who is your devotee is like you; who has the power to fathom you?
By mere conversation for half a moment, he is able to bring [one] across [the worldly ocean].
From fellowship with devotees, there certainly arises [the ability] to practice manifold devotion.
It grows by the sprinkling of water that is the speech of the cloud that is your devotee,
but from the heat of talking with non-devotees, it withers at that very moment.
And from the sprinkling of the remembrance of your qualities, it manifestly grows at that moment.
The sprout of devotion to you, once born, expands greatly in the mind.
It must not be destroyed; it must be nurtured always, always, moment by moment.
Then, having attained the state of Brahman, for the life of the devotee,
[the Lord] truly grants him the fruit, the unsurpassed servitude to Hari.
If, having obtained that rare servitude, one has indeed become a servant,
