that very rare hymn of praise was given to him long ago by Brahmā,
[along with] Hari’s six-syllable mantra and the armour that protects all.
Here it was given at Puṣkara by the pleased Saubhari to him—
that very armour, the hymn of praise, and that very rare mantra—
by that sage, an aṃśa of Brahmā, to Nanda as he was performing austerities.
The mantra, the hymn of praise, the armour, the chosen deity, and the guru—

4.21.s:
yā yasya vidyā prācīnā na tāṃ tyajati niścitam ..
ityevaṃ kathitaṃ stotraṃ śrīkṛṣṇākhyānamadbhutam ..
sukhadaṃ mokṣadaṃ sāraṃ bhavabandhavimocanam .. 233 ..
4.21.d:
या यस्य विद्या प्राचीना न तां त्यजति निश्चितम् ॥
इत्येवं कथितं स्तोत्रं श्रीकृष्णाख्यानमद्भुतम् ॥
सुखदं मोक्षदं सारं भवबन्धविमोचनम् ॥ 233 ॥
4.21.m:
Whatever ancient learning one has, one certainly does not abandon it.
Thus has been recited the hymn of praise, the wondrous narrative of Śrī Kṛṣṇa,
which grants happiness, grants liberation, is the essential truth, and releases from the bondage of worldly existence. 233.

4.22.s:
..śrīnārāyaṇa uvāca ..
ekadā rādhikānātho balena saha bālakaiḥ ..
jagāma tattālavanaṃ paripakvaphalānvitam .. 1 ..
4.22.d:
॥श्रीनारायण उवाच ॥
एकदा राधिकानाथो बलेन सह बालकैः ॥
जगाम तत्तालवनं परिपक्वफलान्वितम् ॥ 1 ॥

4.22.s:
vṛkṣāṇāṃ rakṣitā daityaḥ khara rūpī ca dhenukaḥ..
koṭisiṃhasamabalo devānāṃ darpanāśanaḥ ..2..
4.22.d:
वृक्षाणां रक्षिता दैत्यः खर रूपी च धेनुकः॥
कोटिसिंहसमबलो देवानां दर्पनाशनः ॥2॥

4.22.s:
śarīraṃ parvatasamaṃ kūpatulye ca locane ..
īṣāpaṃktisamā dantāstuṇḍaṃ parvatagahvaram .. 3 ..
4.22.d:
शरीरं पर्वतसमं कूपतुल्ये च लोचने ॥
ईषापंक्तिसमा दन्तास्तुण्डं पर्वतगह्वरम् ॥ 3 ॥

4.22.s:
śatahastaparimitā jihvā lolā bhayānakā ..
kāsārasadṛśī nābhiḥ śabdastasya bhayānakaḥ .. 4 ..
4.22.d:
शतहस्तपरिमिता जिह्वा लोला भयानका ॥
कासारसदृशी नाभिः शब्दस्तस्य भयानकः ॥ 4 ॥

4.22.s:
dṛṣṭvā tālavanaṃ bālā harṣamāpuraninditāḥ ..
kautukātkṛṣṇamūcuste smerānanasaroruhāḥ .. 5 ..
4.22.d:
दृष्ट्वा तालवनं बाला हर्षमापुरनिन्दिताः ॥
कौतुकात्कृष्णमूचुस्ते स्मेराननसरोरुहाः ॥ 5 ॥

4.22.s:
bālā ūcuḥ ..
he kṛṣṇa karuṇāsindho dīna bandho jagatpate ..
mahābala balabhrātaḥ samastabalināṃ vara .. 6 ..
4.22.d:
बाला ऊचुः ॥
हे कृष्ण करुणासिन्धो दीन बन्धो जगत्पते ॥
महाबल बलभ्रातः समस्तबलिनां वर ॥ 6 ॥

4.22.s:
avadhānaṃ kuru vibho kṣaṇārddhaṃ no nivedane ..
kṣudhitānāṃ śiśūnāṃ ca bhaktānāṃ bhaktavatsala .. 7 ..
4.22.d:
अवधानं कुरु विभो क्षणार्द्धं नो निवेदने ॥
क्षुधितानां शिशूनां च भक्तानां भक्तवत्सल ॥ 7 ॥

4.22.s:
svādūni sundarāṇyeva paśya tālaphalāni ca ..
bhaṅktuṃ cālayituṃ vṛkṣānpātituṃ ca phalāni ca .. 8 ..
4.22.d:
स्वादूनि सुन्दराण्येव पश्य तालफलानि च ॥
भङ्क्तुं चालयितुं वृक्षान्पातितुं च फलानि च ॥ 8 ॥

4.22.s:
nānāvarṇāni puṣpāṇi pakvāni durlabhāni ca ..
ājñāṃ karoṣi cetkṛṣṇa ceṣṭāṃ karttu vayaṃ kṣamāḥ ..9..
4.22.d:
नानावर्णानि पुष्पाणि पक्वानि दुर्लभानि च ॥
आज्ञां करोषि चेत्कृष्ण चेष्टां कर्त्तु वयं क्षमाः ॥9॥

4.22.s:
kiṃ tvatra daityo balavānkhararūpī ca dhenukaḥ ..
ajitastridaśaiḥ sarvairmahābalaparākramaḥ .. 4.22.10 ..
4.22.d:
किं त्वत्र दैत्यो बलवान्खररूपी च धेनुकः ॥
अजितस्त्रिदशैः सर्वैर्महाबलपराक्रमः ॥ 4.22.10 ॥

4.22.s:
durnivāryaśca sarveṣāṃ kaṃsasya sacivo mahān ..
hiṃsakaḥ sarvajantūnāṃ vanānāmasti rakṣitā .. 11 ..
4.22.d:
दुर्निवार्यश्च सर्वेषां कंसस्य सचिवो महान् ॥
हिंसकः सर्वजन्तूनां वनानामस्ति रक्षिता ॥ 11 ॥

4.22.s:
suvicārya jagatkānta vada no vadatāṃ vara ..
yuktaṃ kāryamayuktaṃ vā kartavyamatha vā na vā .. 12 ..
4.22.d:
सुविचार्य जगत्कान्त वद नो वदतां वर ॥
युक्तं कार्यमयुक्तं वा कर्तव्यमथ वा न वा ॥ 12 ॥

4.22.s:
bālakānāṃ vacaḥ śrutvā bhagavānmadhusūdanaḥ ..
uvāca madhuraṃ bālānvacanaṃ tatsukhāvaham .. 13 ..
4.22.d:
बालकानां वचः श्रुत्वा भगवान्मधुसूदनः ॥
उवाच मधुरं बालान्वचनं तत्सुखावहम् ॥ 13 ॥

4.22.s:
śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca ..
kiṃ vo daityādbhayaṃ bālā yūyaṃ matsahacāriṇaḥ ..
vṛkṣānbhaṅktvā cālayitvā phalāni khādatābhayam .. 14 ..
4.22.d:
श्रीकृष्ण उवाच ॥
किं वो दैत्याद्भयं बाला यूयं मत्सहचारिणः ॥
वृक्षान्भङ्क्त्वा चालयित्वा फलानि खादताभयम् ॥ 14 ॥

4.22.s:
śrīkṛṣṇājñāṃ samādāya bālakā balaśālinaḥ ..
utpeturvṛkṣaśikharaṃ kṣudhitāśca phalārthinaḥ .. 15 ..
4.22.d:
श्रीकृष्णाज्ञां समादाय बालका बलशालिनः ॥
उत्पेतुर्वृक्षशिखरं क्षुधिताश्च फलार्थिनः ॥ 15 ॥

4.22.s:
nānāprakāravarṇāni svādūni sundarāṇi ca ..
phalāni pātayāmāsuḥ paripakvāni nārada .. 16 ..
4.22.d:
नानाप्रकारवर्णानि स्वादूनि सुन्दराणि च ॥
फलानि पातयामासुः परिपक्वानि नारद ॥ 16 ॥

4.22.s:
kecidbabhañjurvṛkṣāśca cālayāmāsureva ca ..
kecitkolāhalaṃ cakurnanṛtustatra kecana .. 17 ..
4.22.d:
केचिद्बभञ्जुर्वृक्षाश्च चालयामासुरेव च ॥
केचित्कोलाहलं चकुर्ननृतुस्तत्र केचन ॥ 17 ॥

4.22.s:
avaruhya tarubhyaśca bālakā balaśālinaḥ ..
phalānyādāya gacchanto dadṛśurdaityapuṅgavam .. 18 ..
4.22.d:
अवरुह्य तरुभ्यश्च बालका बलशालिनः ॥
फलान्यादाय गच्छन्तो ददृशुर्दैत्यपुङ्गवम् ॥ 18 ॥

4.22.s:
mahābalaṃ mahākāyaṃ ghoraṃ gardabharūpiṇam ..
āgacchantaṃ mahāvegātkurvantaṃ śabdamulbaṇam .. 19 ..
4.22.d:
महाबलं महाकायं घोरं गर्दभरूपिणम् ॥
आगच्छन्तं महावेगात्कुर्वन्तं शब्दमुल्बणम् ॥ 19 ॥

4.22.s:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā ruruduḥ sarve phalāni tatyajurbhiyā ..
kṛṣṇakṛṣṇeti śabdaṃ ca pracakrurbahudhā bhṛśam .. 4.22.20 ..
4.22.d:
तं दृष्ट्वा रुरुदुः सर्वे फलानि तत्यजुर्भिया ॥
कृष्णकृष्णेति शब्दं च प्रचक्रुर्बहुधा भृशम् ॥ 4.22.20 ॥

4.22.s:
asmānrakṣa samāgaccha he kṛṣṇa karuṇānidhe ..
he saṅkarṣaṇa no rakṣa prāṇā no yānti dānavāt..21..
4.22.d:
अस्मान्रक्ष समागच्छ हे कृष्ण करुणानिधे ॥
हे सङ्कर्षण नो रक्ष प्राणा नो यान्ति दानवात्॥21॥

4.22.s:
he kṛṣṇa he kṛṣṇa hare murāre govinda dāmodara dīnabandho..
gopīśagopeśa bhavārṇave'smā nananta nārāyaṇa rakṣa rakṣa ..22..
4.22.d:
हे कृष्ण हे कृष्ण हरे मुरारे गोविन्द दामोदर दीनबन्धो॥
गोपीशगोपेश भवार्णवेऽस्मा ननन्त नारायण रक्ष रक्ष ॥22॥

4.22.s:
bhaye'bhaye vātha śubhe'śubhe vā sukheṣu duḥkheṣu ca dīnanātha ..
tvayā vinā'nyaṃ śaraṇaṃ bhavārṇave na no'sti he mādhava rakṣa rakṣa..23..
4.22.d:
भयेऽभये वाथ शुभेऽशुभे वा सुखेषु दुःखेषु च दीननाथ ॥
त्वया विनाऽन्यं शरणं भवार्णवे न नोऽस्ति हे माधव रक्ष रक्ष॥23॥

4.22.s:
jayajaya guṇasindho kṛṣṇa bhaktaikabandho bahutarabhayayuktānbālakānrakṣa rakṣa ..
jahi danujakulānāmīśamasmāka mantaṃ surakulabaladarpaṃ vardhayemaṃ nihatya .. 24 ..
4.22.d:
जयजय गुणसिन्धो कृष्ण भक्तैकबन्धो बहुतरभययुक्तान्बालकान्रक्ष रक्ष ॥
जहि दनुजकुलानामीशमस्माक मन्तं सुरकुलबलदर्पं वर्धयेमं निहत्य ॥ 24 ॥

4.22.s:
bālānāṃ viklavaṃ dṛṣṭvā balena saha mādhavaḥ ..
ājagāma śiśusthānaṃ bhayahā bhakta vatsalaḥ .. 25 ..
4.22.d:
बालानां विक्लवं दृष्ट्वा बलेन सह माधवः ॥
आजगाम शिशुस्थानं भयहा भक्त वत्सलः ॥ 25 ॥

4.22.s:
bhayaṃ nāsti bhayaṃ nāstītyuktvā dudrāva satvaram ..
īṣaddhāsyaprasannāsyo nirbhayaṃ dattavāñchiśūn .. 26 ..
4.22.d:
भयं नास्ति भयं नास्तीत्युक्त्वा दुद्राव सत्वरम् ॥
ईषद्धास्यप्रसन्नास्यो निर्भयं दत्तवाञ्छिशून् ॥ 26 ॥

4.22.s:
dṛṣṭvā kṛṣṇaṃ balaṃ bālā nanṛturvijahurbhayam ..
harismṛtiścābhayadā sarvamaṅgaladāyikā..27..
4.22.d:
दृष्ट्वा कृष्णं बलं बाला ननृतुर्विजहुर्भयम् ॥
हरिस्मृतिश्चाभयदा सर्वमङ्गलदायिका॥27॥

4.22.s:
śrīkṛṣṇo dānavaṃ dṛṣṭvā grasantaṃ purataḥ śiśūn..
balaṃ saṃbodhya balinamuvāca madhusūdanaḥ .. 28 ..
4.22.d:
श्रीकृष्णो दानवं दृष्ट्वा ग्रसन्तं पुरतः शिशून्॥
बलं संबोध्य बलिनमुवाच मधुसूदनः ॥ 28 ॥

4.22.s:
śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca ..
dānavo baliputro'yaṃ nāmnā sāhasiko balī ..
gardabho brahmaśāpena śapto durvāsasā purā ..29..
4.22.d:
श्रीकृष्ण उवाच ॥
दानवो बलिपुत्रोऽयं नाम्ना साहसिको बली ॥
गर्दभो ब्रह्मशापेन शप्तो दुर्वाससा पुरा ॥29॥

4.22.s:
pāpiṣṭho mama vadhyo'yaṃ mahābalaparākamaḥ ..
ahamenaṃ vadhiṣyāmi tvaṃ rakṣa bālakānbala ..4.22.30..
4.22.d:
पापिष्ठो मम वध्योऽयं महाबलपराकमः ॥
अहमेनं वधिष्यामि त्वं रक्ष बालकान्बल ॥4.22.30॥
4.22.m:
This most wicked one, possessing great strength and prowess, is to be slain by me.
I shall slay him; protect the boys, O Bala! (30)

4.22.s:
ādāya bālakānsarvāndūraṃ gacchetyuvāca ha ..
tāngṛhītvā balaḥ śīghraṃ jagāma tvarayājñayā .. 31 ..
4.22.d:
आदाय बालकान्सर्वान्दूरं गच्छेत्युवाच ह ॥
तान्गृहीत्वा बलः शीघ्रं जगाम त्वरयाज्ञया ॥ 31 ॥
4.22.m:
Taking all the boys, go far away!" so indeed he spoke.
Taking them, Bala quickly departed in haste according to his command. (31)

4.22.s:
dṛṣṭvā kṛṣṇaṃ dānavendro mahābalaparākramaḥ ..
jagrāsa līlayā kopājjvaladagniśikhopamam .. 32 ..
4.22.d:
दृष्ट्वा कृष्णं दानवेन्द्रो महाबलपराक्रमः ॥
जग्रास लीलया कोपाज्ज्वलदग्निशिखोपमम् ॥ 32 ॥
4.22.m:
Seeing Kṛṣṇa, the lord of Dānavas, endowed with great strength and prowess,
swallowed him playfully in wrath, him who was like a blazing flame of fire. (32)

4.22.s:
babhūvātidāhayukto martukāmo'titejasā ..
ujjagrāsa punardaityo vibhuṃ tejasvinaṃ bhiyā ..33..
4.22.d:
बभूवातिदाहयुक्तो मर्तुकामोऽतितेजसा ॥
उज्जग्रास पुनर्दैत्यो विभुं तेजस्विनं भिया ॥33॥
4.22.m:
He was filled with extreme burning, desiring to die on account of [Kṛṣṇa's] immense splendor;
in fear, the Daitya vomited forth the all-pervading, radiant Lord again. (33)

4.22.s:
ujjhitaṃ santamīśaṃ ca dṛṣṭvā daityo mumoca ha..
atīva sundaraṃ śāntaṃ jvalantaṃ brahmatejasā ..34..
4.22.d:
उज्झितं सन्तमीशं च दृष्ट्वा दैत्यो मुमोच ह॥
अतीव सुन्दरं शान्तं ज्वलन्तं ब्रह्मतेजसा ॥34॥
4.22.m:
And seeing the Lord expelled and peaceful, the Daitya released him,
exceedingly handsome, serene, and blazing with the luster of Brahman. (34)

4.22.s:
kṛṣṇadarśanamātreṇa babhūvāsya purā smṛtiḥ ..
ātmānaṃ bubudhe kṛṣṇaṃ jagatāṃ kāraṇaṃ param .. 35 ..
4.22.d:
कृष्णदर्शनमात्रेण बभूवास्य पुरा स्मृतिः ॥
आत्मानं बुबुधे कृष्णं जगतां कारणं परम् ॥ 35 ॥
4.22.m:
Merely upon the sight of Kṛṣṇa, his remembrance of the past returned;
he recognized himself and [recognized] Kṛṣṇa as the supreme cause of the worlds. (35)

4.22.s:
tejaḥsvarūpamīśaṃ taṃ dṛṣṭvā tuṣṭāva dānavaḥ ..
yathāgamaṃ yathājanma guṇātītaṃ śruteḥ param .. 36 ..
4.22.d:
तेजःस्वरूपमीशं तं दृष्ट्वा तुष्टाव दानवः ॥
यथागमं यथाजन्म गुणातीतं श्रुतेः परम् ॥ 36 ॥
4.22.m:
Seeing that Lord whose form is light, the Dānava praised him
according to tradition, according to his birth, him who is beyond the gunas and beyond the Vedas: (36)

4.22.s:
dānava uvāca ..
vāmano'si tvamaṃśena matpituryajñabhikṣukaḥ ..
rājyahartā ca śrīhartā sutalasthaladāyakaḥ .. 37 ..
4.22.d:
दानव उवाच ॥
वामनोऽसि त्वमंशेन मत्पितुर्यज्ञभिक्षुकः ॥
राज्यहर्ता च श्रीहर्ता सुतलस्थलदायकः ॥ 37 ॥
4.22.m:
"You are Vāmana in a portion, a beggar at my father's sacrifice,
the taker of his kingdom and taker of his fortune, the giver of the realm of Sutala. (37)

4.22.s:
balirbhaktivaśo vīraḥ sarveśo bhaktavatsalaḥ ..
śīghraṃ tvaṃ hindhi māṃ pāpaṃ śāpādgardabharūpiṇam .. 38 ..
4.22.d:
बलिर्भक्तिवशो वीरः सर्वेशो भक्तवत्सलः ॥
शीघ्रं त्वं हिन्धि मां पापं शापाद्गर्दभरूपिणम् ॥ 38 ॥
4.22.m:
Bali was subdued by devotion, a hero; [you are] the Lord of all, fond of your devotees.
Quickly slay me, a sinner in the form of a donkey through a curse! (38)

4.22.s:
munerdurvāsasaḥ śāpādīdṛśaṃ janma kutsitam ..
mṛtyuruktaśca muninā tvatto mama jagatpate .. 39 ..
4.22.d:
मुनेर्दुर्वाससः शापादीदृशं जन्म कुत्सितम् ॥
मृत्युरुक्तश्च मुनिना त्वत्तो मम जगत्पते ॥ 39 ॥
4.22.m:
Such a contemptible birth was brought about by the curse of the sage Durvāsas,
and my death was declared by the sage to be from you, O Lord of the universe! (39)

4.22.s:
ṣoḍaśāreṇa cakreṇa sutīkṣṇenātitejasā ..
jahi māṃ jagatāṃ nātha sadbhaktiṃ kuru mokṣada ..4.22.40..
4.22.d:
षोडशारेण चक्रेण सुतीक्ष्णेनातितेजसा ॥
जहि मां जगतां नाथ सद्भक्तिं कुरु मोक्षद ॥4.22.40॥
4.22.m:
With your sixteen-spoked discus, exceedingly sharp and immensely brilliant,
slay me, O Lord of the worlds, and grant true devotion, O giver of liberation! (40)

4.22.s:
tvamaṃśena varāhaśca samuddhartuṃ vasundharām ..
vedānāṃ rakṣitā nātha hiraṇyākṣaniṣūdanaḥ .. 41 ..
4.22.d:
त्वमंशेन वराहश्च समुद्धर्तुं वसुन्धराम् ॥
वेदानां रक्षिता नाथ हिरण्याक्षनिषूदनः ॥ 41 ॥
4.22.m:
You were also the Boar in a portion to uplift the earth,
the protector of the Vedas, O Lord, the slayer of Hiraṇyākṣa. (41)

4.22.s:
tvaṃ nṛsiṃhaḥ svayaṃ pūrṇo hiraṇyakaśiporvadhe ..
prahrādānugrahārthāya devānāṃ rakṣaṇāya ca .. .. 42 ..
4.22.d:
त्वं नृसिंहः स्वयं पूर्णो हिरण्यकशिपोर्वधे ॥
प्रह्रादानुग्रहार्थाय देवानां रक्षणाय च ॥ ॥ 42 ॥
4.22.m:
You yourself were Nṛsiṃha in fullness at the slaying of Hiraṇyakaśipu,
for the sake of bestowing grace upon Prahrāda and for the protection of the gods. (42)

4.22.s:
tvaṃ ca vedoddhārakartā mīnāṃśena dayānidhe ..
nṛpasya jñānadānāya rakṣāyai suraviprayoḥ .. 43 ..
4.22.d:
त्वं च वेदोद्धारकर्ता मीनांशेन दयानिधे ॥
नृपस्य ज्ञानदानाय रक्षायै सुरविप्रयोः ॥ 43 ॥
4.22.m:
And you were the rescuer of the Vedas through a portion as the Fish, O ocean of compassion,
to bestow knowledge upon the king and to protect the gods and the brāhmaṇa. (43)

4.22.s:
śeṣādhāraśca kūrmastvamaṃśena sṛṣṭihetave ..
viśvādhāraśca viśvastvamaṃśenāpi sahasradhṛk ..44..
4.22.d:
शेषाधारश्च कूर्मस्त्वमंशेन सृष्टिहेतवे ॥
विश्वाधारश्च विश्वस्त्वमंशेनापि सहस्रधृक् ॥44॥
4.22.m:
And you were the Tortoise, the support of Śeṣa, in a portion for the purpose of creation;
and you are the support of the universe and the universe itself, the thousand-bearer, through a portion. (44)

4.22.s:
rāmo dāśarathistvaṃ ca jānakyuddhārahetave ..
daśakandharahantā ca sindhau setuvidhāyakaḥ ..45..
4.22.d:
रामो दाशरथिस्त्वं च जानक्युद्धारहेतवे ॥
दशकन्धरहन्ता च सिन्धौ सेतुविधायकः ॥45॥
4.22.m:
And you were Rāma, the son of Daśaratha, for the purpose of rescuing Jānakī,
the slayer of the ten-necked [Rāvaṇa], the builder of the bridge across the ocean. (45)

4.22.s:
kalayā paraśurāmaśca jamadagnisuto mahān ..
triḥsaptakṛtvo bhūpānāṃ nihantā jagatīpate .. 46 ..
4.22.d:
कलया परशुरामश्च जमदग्निसुतो महान् ॥
त्रिःसप्तकृत्वो भूपानां निहन्ता जगतीपते ॥ 46 ॥
4.22.m:
And as Paraśurāma by a part, the great son of Jamadagni,
the slayer of the kings thrice seven times, O Lord of the earth! (46)

4.22.s:
aṃśena kapilastvaṃ ca siddhānāṃ ca gurorguruḥ ..
mātṛjñānapradātā ca yogaśāstravidhāyakaḥ .. 47 ..
4.22.d:
अंशेन कपिलस्त्वं च सिद्धानां च गुरोर्गुरुः ॥
मातृज्ञानप्रदाता च योगशास्त्रविधायकः ॥ 47 ॥
4.22.m:
And you were Kapila through a portion, the guru of the guru of the perfected ones,
the giver of knowledge to your mother, the author of the treatise on Yoga. (47)

4.22.s:
aṃśena jñānināṃ śreṣṭho naranārāyaṇāvṛṣī ..
tvaṃ ca dharmasuto bhūtvā lokavistārakārakaḥ ..48..
4.22.d:
अंशेन ज्ञानिनां श्रेष्ठो नरनारायणावृषी ॥
त्वं च धर्मसुतो भूत्वा लोकविस्तारकारकः ॥48॥
4.22.m:
Through a portion, [you became] the two sages Nara and Nārāyaṇa, the best of the wise;
and becoming the son of Dharma, you expanded the worlds. (48)

4.22.s:
adhunā kṛṣṇarūpastvaṃ paripūrṇatamaḥ svayam ..
sarveṣāmavatārāṇāṃ bījarūpaḥ sanātanaḥ .. 49 ..
4.22.d:
अधुना कृष्णरूपस्त्वं परिपूर्णतमः स्वयम् ॥
सर्वेषामवताराणां बीजरूपः सनातनः ॥ 49 ॥
4.22.m:
Now, you are in the form of Kṛṣṇa, the most complete yourself,
the eternal seed-form of all incarnations, (49)

4.22.s:
yaśodājīvano nityo nandaikānandavardhanaḥ ..
prāṇādhidevo gopīnāṃ rādhāprāṇādhikapriyaḥ ..4.22.50..
4.22.d:
यशोदाजीवनो नित्यो नन्दैकानन्दवर्धनः ॥
प्राणाधिदेवो गोपीनां राधाप्राणाधिकप्रियः ॥4.22.50॥
4.22.m:
the life of Yaśodā, eternal, the sole increaser of Nanda's joy,
the presiding deity of the life-breaths of the gopīs, dearer to Rādhā than her own life-breath, (50)

4.22.s:
vasudevasutaḥ śānto devakīduḥkhabhañjanaḥ ..
ayonisaṃbhavaḥ śrīmānpṛthivībhārahārakaḥ .. 51 ..
4.22.d:
वसुदेवसुतः शान्तो देवकीदुःखभञ्जनः ॥
अयोनिसंभवः श्रीमान्पृथिवीभारहारकः ॥ 51 ॥
4.22.m:
the son of Vasudeva, serene, the shatterer of Devakī's sorrow,
not born of a womb, glorious, the remover of the earth's burden, (51)

4.22.s:
pūtanāyai mātṛgatiṃ pradātā ca kṛpānidhiḥ ..
bakakeśipralambānāṃ mamāpi mokṣakārakaḥ .. 52 ..
4.22.d:
पूतनायै मातृगतिं प्रदाता च कृपानिधिः ॥
बककेशिप्रलम्बानां ममापि मोक्षकारकः ॥ 52 ॥
4.22.m:
the giver of the state of a mother to Pūtanā, an ocean of mercy,
the cause of liberation for Baka, Keśin, and Pralamba, and for me as well. (52)

4.22.s:
svecchāmaya guṇātīta bhaktānāṃ bhayabhañjana ..
prasīda rādhikānātha prasīda kuru mokṣaṇam .. ..53..
4.22.d:
स्वेच्छामय गुणातीत भक्तानां भयभञ्जन ॥
प्रसीद राधिकानाथ प्रसीद कुरु मोक्षणम् ॥ ॥53॥
4.22.m:
O you whose will is your only law, beyond the gunas, shatterer of the fear of devotees,
be gracious, O Lord of Rādhikā, be gracious, grant release! (53)

4.22.s:
he nātha gārdabhīyoneḥ samuddhara bhavārṇavāt..
mūrkhastvadbhaktaputro'haṃ māmuddhartuṃ tvamarhasi .. 54 ..
4.22.d:
हे नाथ गार्दभीयोनेः समुद्धर भवार्णवात्॥
मूर्खस्त्वद्भक्तपुत्रोऽहं मामुद्धर्तुं त्वमर्हसि ॥ 54 ॥
4.22.m:
O Lord, deliver me from the womb of a donkey, from the ocean of worldly existence!
I am a fool, the son of your devotee; you ought to deliver me. (54)

4.22.s:
vedā brahmādayo yaṃ ca munīndrāḥ stotumakṣamāḥ ..
kiṃ staumi taṃ guṇātītaṃ purā daityo'dhunā kharaḥ ..55..
4.22.d:
वेदा ब्रह्मादयो यं च मुनीन्द्राः स्तोतुमक्षमाः ॥
किं स्तौमि तं गुणातीतं पुरा दैत्योऽधुना खरः ॥55॥
4.22.m:
He whom the Vedas, Brahmā and the others, and the foremost sages are unable to praise,
how can I praise him, beyond the gunas—I, formerly a Daitya, now an ass? (55)

4.22.s:
evaṃ kuru kṛpāsindho yena me na bhavejjanuḥ ..
dṛṣṭvā pādāravindaṃ te kaḥ punarbhavanaṃ vrajet ..56..
4.22.d:
एवं कुरु कृपासिन्धो येन मे न भवेज्जनुः ॥
दृष्ट्वा पादारविन्दं ते कः पुनर्भवनं व्रजेत् ॥56॥
4.22.m:
Act thus, O ocean of mercy, so that I may have no rebirth!"
Having seen your lotus feet, who would return to worldly existence?

4.22.s:
brahmā stotā kharaḥ stotā nopahāsitumarhasi..
sadīśvarasya vijñasya yogyāyogye samā kṛpā .. 57 ..
4.22.d:
ब्रह्मा स्तोता खरः स्तोता नोपहासितुमर्हसि॥
सदीश्वरस्य विज्ञस्य योग्यायोग्ये समा कृपा ॥ 57 ॥
4.22.m:
Brahmā is a praiser, an ass is a praiser—you ought not to mock [me].
To the true Lord who is omniscient, grace is equal toward the worthy and the unworthy.

4.22.s:
ityevamuktvā daityendrastasthau ca purato hareḥ ..
prasannavadanaḥ śrīmānatituṣṭo babhūva ha ..58..
4.22.d:
इत्येवमुक्त्वा दैत्येन्द्रस्तस्थौ च पुरतो हरेः ॥
प्रसन्नवदनः श्रीमानतितुष्टो बभूव ह ॥58॥
4.22.m:
Having spoken thus, the lord of the Daityas stood before Hari;
with a cheerful face and glorious, he became exceedingly delighted.

4.22.s:
idaṃ daityakṛtaṃ stotraṃ nityaṃ bhaktyā ca yaḥ paṭhet ..
sālokyasārṣṭisāmīpyaṃ līlayā labhate hareḥ..59..
4.22.d:
इदं दैत्यकृतं स्तोत्रं नित्यं भक्त्या च यः पठेत् ॥
सालोक्यसार्ष्टिसामीप्यं लीलया लभते हरेः॥59॥
4.22.m:
Whoever recites daily with devotion this hymn of praise composed by the Daitya,
effortlessly attains residence in Hari's realm, equal power, and proximity to Hari.

4.22.s:
iha loke harerbhaktimante dāsyaṃ sudurlabham..
vidyāṃ śriyaṃ sukavitāṃ putrapautrānyaśo labhet .. 4.22.60 ..
4.22.d:
इह लोके हरेर्भक्तिमन्ते दास्यं सुदुर्लभम्॥
विद्यां श्रियं सुकवितां पुत्रपौत्रान्यशो लभेत् ॥ 4.22.60 ॥
4.22.m:
In this world [he attains] devotion to Hari, and in the end very rare servitude [to him];
he obtains knowledge, fortune, poetic skill, sons, grandsons, and fame.

4.22.s:
śrīnārāyaṇa uvāca ..
śrutvā'numene daityendrastavanaṃ karuṇānidhiḥ ..
kathaṃ karomi saṃhāramīdṛśaṃ bhaktamityaho .. ..61..
4.22.d:
श्रीनारायण उवाच ॥
श्रुत्वाऽनुमेने दैत्येन्द्रस्तवनं करुणानिधिः ॥
कथं करोमि संहारमीदृशं भक्तमित्यहो ॥ ॥61॥
4.22.m:
Hearing [it], the storehouse of compassion approved the praise by the lord of the Daityas;
“How can I bring about the destruction of such a devotee? Ah!”

4.22.s:
anumanya smṛtiṃ tasya saṃjahāra hariḥ svayam ..
na hi yukto vadhaḥ stoturdurvakturvidhirīśvarāt ..62..
4.22.d:
अनुमन्य स्मृतिं तस्य संजहार हरिः स्वयम् ॥
न हि युक्तो वधः स्तोतुर्दुर्वक्तुर्विधिरीश्वरात् ॥62॥
4.22.m:
Having approved, Hari himself took away his recollection;
for the killing of a praiser is not proper—an ordained act from the Lord applies to a wicked speaker.

4.22.s:
dānavo māyayā viṣṇorvisasmāra punaḥ svakam..
duruktistatkaṇṭhadeśe hyadhiṣṭhānaṃ cakāra ha..63..
4.22.d:
दानवो मायया विष्णोर्विसस्मार पुनः स्वकम्॥
दुरुक्तिस्तत्कण्ठदेशे ह्यधिष्ठानं चकार ह॥63॥
4.22.m:
Through Viṣṇu's māyā, the Dānava forgot his own [state] once again;
indeed, harsh speech took up residence in the region of his throat.

4.22.s:
uvāca śrīhariṃ daityaḥ kopātprasphuritādharaḥ ..
mune sadyo martukāmo daivagrasto vicetanaḥ ..64..
4.22.d:
उवाच श्रीहरिं दैत्यः कोपात्प्रस्फुरिताधरः ॥
मुने सद्यो मर्तुकामो दैवग्रस्तो विचेतनः ॥64॥
4.22.m:
With his lip quivering in anger, the Daitya spoke to Śrī Hari,
O sage, desiring immediate death, seized by fate, and devoid of sense:

4.22.s:
daitya uvāca.. dhruvaṃ tvaṃ martukāmo'si durbuddhe mānavārbhaka ..
adya prasthāpayiṣyāmi tvāmahaṃ yamamandiram .. ..65..
4.22.d:
दैत्य उवाच॥ ध्रुवं त्वं मर्तुकामोऽसि दुर्बुद्धे मानवार्भक ॥
अद्य प्रस्थापयिष्यामि त्वामहं यममन्दिरम् ॥ ॥65॥
4.22.m:
The Daitya said: / “Certainly you wish to die, O evil-minded human boy!
Today I will dispatch you to the abode of Yama.

4.22.s:
āyāsi jīvanākāṅkṣī mama tālavanaṃ śiśo..
na yāsyasi punargehaṃ bāndhavaṃ na hi drakṣyasi ..66..
4.22.d:
आयासि जीवनाकाङ्क्षी मम तालवनं शिशो॥
न यास्यसि पुनर्गेहं बान्धवं न हि द्रक्ष्यसि ॥66॥
4.22.m:
Desiring your life, did you come to my palm forest, boy?
You shall not return to your home, nor indeed will you see your relatives.

4.22.s:
na kaṃso na jarāsandho narako na samo mama ..
devāḥ kampanti me nityaṃ ke cānye matsamā bhuvi ..67..
4.22.d:
न कंसो न जरासन्धो नरको न समो मम ॥
देवाः कम्पन्ति मे नित्यं के चान्ये मत्समा भुवि ॥67॥
4.22.m:
Neither Kaṃsa, nor Jarāsandha, nor Naraka is equal to me.
The gods tremble before me constantly; and who else on earth is my equal?

4.22.s:
nahi saṃhārakartā ca māṃ saṃhartuṃ kṣamaḥ śivaḥ ..
na ca brahmā na viṣṇuśca na mṛtyuḥ kāla eva ca ..68..
4.22.d:
नहि संहारकर्ता च मां संहर्तुं क्षमः शिवः ॥
न च ब्रह्मा न विष्णुश्च न मृत्युः काल एव च ॥68॥
4.22.m:
Even Śiva, the author of destruction, is not capable of destroying me,
nor Brahmā, nor Viṣṇu, nor death, nor Time itself.

4.22.s:
mama tālatarūnbhaṅktvā pātayitvā phalāni ca ..
ahaṃkaroṣi sahasā kimaho kasya tejasā .. 69 ..
4.22.d:
मम तालतरून्भङ्क्त्वा पातयित्वा फलानि च ॥
अहंकरोषि सहसा किमहो कस्य तेजसा ॥ 69 ॥
4.22.m:
Having broken my palm trees and knocked down the fruits,
why, ah, by whose prowess do you suddenly act with arrogance?

4.22.s:
kastvaṃ vada baṭo satyaṃ kamanīyo'tisundaraḥ ..
durlabhaṃ jīvanaṃ dātuṃ mahyaṃ kathamihāgataḥ ..4.22.70 ..
4.22.d:
कस्त्वं वद बटो सत्यं कमनीयोऽतिसुन्दरः ॥
दुर्लभं जीवनं दातुं मह्यं कथमिहागतः ॥4.22.70 ॥
4.22.m:
Speak the truth, boy, who are you, so lovely and exceedingly handsome?
How have you come here to give up your life, which is hard to obtain?”

4.22.s:
ityuktvā mastake kṛtvā prerayitvā tu taṃ balī ..
dūrataḥ pātayāmāsa śrīkṛṣṇaṃ maraṇonmukhaḥ .. 71 ..
4.22.d:
इत्युक्त्वा मस्तके कृत्वा प्रेरयित्वा तु तं बली ॥
दूरतः पातयामास श्रीकृष्णं मरणोन्मुखः ॥ 71 ॥
4.22.m:
Having said this, the mighty one placed [him] on his head, propelled him,
and hurled Śrī Kṛṣṇa far away, heading toward his own death.

4.22.s:
pātayitvā ca taṃ bhūmau viṣāṇābhyāṃ jaghāna saḥ ..
kṛṣṇāṅgasparśamātreṇa tadviṣāṇe babhañjatuḥ ..72..
4.22.d:
पातयित्वा च तं भूमौ विषाणाभ्यां जघान सः ॥
कृष्णाङ्गस्पर्शमात्रेण तद्विषाणे बभञ्जतुः ॥72॥
4.22.m:
And having thrown him down onto the ground, he struck him with his two horns;
at the mere touch of Kṛṣṇa's limb, those two horns broke.

4.22.s:
daityo bhagnaviṣāṇaśca tamīśaṃ kopayanmune ..
jagrāsa carvaṇaṃ kartuṃ bhagnadanto babhūva ha .. 73 ..
4.22.d:
दैत्यो भग्नविषाणश्च तमीशं कोपयन्मुने ॥
जग्रास चर्वणं कर्तुं भग्नदन्तो बभूव ह ॥ 73 ॥
4.22.m:
His horns broken, the Daitya, enraging the Lord, O sage,
swallowed him to chew him, but his teeth broke.

4.22.s:
tejasā dagdhavaktraśca tamujjagrāha tatkṣaṇe ..
jajvāla vyathitaḥ kopāddadāra khurato mahīm .. 74 ..
4.22.d:
तेजसा दग्धवक्त्रश्च तमुज्जग्राह तत्क्षणे ॥
जज्वाल व्यथितः कोपाद्ददार खुरतो महीम् ॥ 74 ॥
4.22.m:
His mouth burnt by [Kṛṣṇa's] splendor, he vomited him out at that moment;
agonized, he blazed with rage, and tore the earth with his hoof.

4.22.s:
cūrṇayitvā tu lāṃgūlaṃ śabdaṃ kṛtvā bhayānakam ..
sa jagāma śiśusthānaṃ dudruvurbālakā bhiyā .. 79..
4.22.d:
चूर्णयित्वा तु लांगूलं शब्दं कृत्वा भयानकम् ॥
स जगाम शिशुस्थानं दुद्रुवुर्बालका भिया ॥ 79॥
4.22.m:
Thrashing his tail and making a terrifying sound,
he went to the place of the children; the boys ran away in fear.

4.22.s:
balaṃ ca prerayāmāsa mastakena mahābalī ..
balo muṣṭiṃ dadau tasmai mūrcchāmāpa tato'suraḥ ..76..
4.22.d:
बलं च प्रेरयामास मस्तकेन महाबली ॥
बलो मुष्टिं ददौ तस्मै मूर्च्छामाप ततोऽसुरः ॥76॥
4.22.m:
The very powerful one charged Bala with his head;
Bala struck him with his fist; thereupon the Asura fell unconscious.

4.22.s:
kṣaṇena cetanāṃ prāpya jagāma harisannidhim ..
balamuṣṭyā ca vyathitaḥ punarmūrcchāmavāpa saḥ .. 77 ..
4.22.d:
क्षणेन चेतनां प्राप्य जगाम हरिसन्निधिम् ॥
बलमुष्ट्या च व्यथितः पुनर्मूर्च्छामवाप सः ॥ 77 ॥
4.22.m:
Recovering consciousness in an instant, he went into the presence of Hari;
pained by Bala's fist, he fainted once again.

4.22.s:
punaśca cetanāṃ prāpya samuttasthau vyathākulaḥ ..
utsasarja bṛhalleḍaṃ mūtraṃ ca bhayamāpa ha ..78..
4.22.d:
पुनश्च चेतनां प्राप्य समुत्तस्थौ व्यथाकुलः ॥
उत्ससर्ज बृहल्लेडं मूत्रं च भयमाप ह ॥78॥
4.22.m:
And regaining consciousness again, he rose up, agitated with pain;
he discharged copious dung and urine, and felt fear.

4.22.s:
kṣaṇātsaṃdhikṣaṇaṃ prāpya mahābalaparākramaḥ ..
kṛtvā śirasi govindaṃ cūrṇayāmāsa dānavaḥ .. 79 ..
4.22.d:
क्षणात्संधिक्षणं प्राप्य महाबलपराक्रमः ॥
कृत्वा शिरसि गोविन्दं चूर्णयामास दानवः ॥ 79 ॥
4.22.m:
Finding an opening after a moment, endowed with great strength and valor,
the Dānava placed Govinda on his head and crushed him;

4.22.s:
pātayāmāsa bhūmau taṃ cūrṇayitvā punaḥpunaḥ ..
utpāṭya tālavṛkṣaṃ taṃ tāḍayāmāsa mādhavaḥ ..4.22.80..
4.22.d:
पातयामास भूमौ तं चूर्णयित्वा पुनःपुनः ॥
उत्पाट्य तालवृक्षं तं ताडयामास माधवः ॥4.22.80॥
4.22.m:
having crushed him repeatedly, he threw him down onto the ground.
Uprooting a palm tree, Mādhava struck him.

4.22.s:
yathā khaḍgaprahāreṇa dānavasya bhavedvyathā ..
tathā babhūva daityasya tālavṛkṣasya tāḍanāt ..81.. .
4.22.d:
यथा खड्गप्रहारेण दानवस्य भवेद्व्यथा ॥
तथा बभूव दैत्यस्य तालवृक्षस्य ताडनात् ॥81॥ ।
4.22.m:
Just as pain would be caused to a Dānava by the blow of a sword,
so it happened to the Daitya from the strike of the palm tree. / Uprooting Govardhana, the Lord struck him;

4.22.s:
govardhanaṃ samutpāṭya ghātayāmāsa taṃ vibhuḥ ..
papāta vegācchailendrastasyopari mahāmune ..82..
4.22.d:
गोवर्धनं समुत्पाट्य घातयामास तं विभुः ॥
पपात वेगाच्छैलेन्द्रस्तस्योपरि महामुने ॥82॥
4.22.m: the king of mountains fell with speed upon him, O great sage.

4.22.s:
parvatasya prahāreṇa mūrcchāmāpa mahābalaḥ.. .
babhūva jarjarāṅgaśca rudhiraṃ ca samudvaman .. 83 ..
4.22.d:
पर्वतस्य प्रहारेण मूर्च्छामाप महाबलः॥ ।
बभूव जर्जराङ्गश्च रुधिरं च समुद्वमन् ॥ 83 ॥
4.22.m: Under the blow of the mountain, the very powerful one fainted; / his limbs were battered, and he vomited blood.

4.22.s:
kṣaṇena cetanāṃ prāpya samuttasthau ruṣā'suraḥ ..
gṛhītvā parvataśreṣṭhaṃ prerayāmāsa mādhavam . .. 84 ..
4.22.d:
क्षणेन चेतनां प्राप्य समुत्तस्थौ रुषाऽसुरः ॥
गृहीत्वा पर्वतश्रेष्ठं प्रेरयामास माधवम् ॥। 84 ॥
4.22.m:
Recovering consciousness in an instant, the Asura rose up in anger;
seizing the excellent mountain, he hurled it at Mādhava.

4.22.s:
dṛṣṭvā śailamutpatantaṃ vegena madhusūdanaḥ ..
jagrāha dakṣiṇakare yathekṣudaṇḍavatprabhuḥ .. 85 ..
4.22.d:
दृष्ट्वा शैलमुत्पतन्तं वेगेन मधुसूदनः ॥
जग्राह दक्षिणकरे यथेक्षुदण्डवत्प्रभुः ॥ 85 ॥
4.22.m:
Seeing the mountain flying swiftly, Madhusūdana,
the Lord, caught it in his right hand like a stalk of sugarcane;

4.22.s:
pūrvasthāne parvataṃ taṃ sthāpayāmāsa kautukāt ..
gṛhītvā daityakarṇāgraṃ pātayāmāsa dūrataḥ .. 86 ..
4.22.d:
पूर्वस्थाने पर्वतं तं स्थापयामास कौतुकात् ॥
गृहीत्वा दैत्यकर्णाग्रं पातयामास दूरतः ॥ 86 ॥
4.22.m:
he placed that mountain in its former location in sport;
and grasping the tip of the Daitya's ear, he threw him far away.

4.22.s:
utpatya ca mahāvegāccakāra veṣṭanaṃ hareḥ ..
pṛthivīṃ gharṣayāmāsa tīkṣṇāgreṇa khureṇa ca .. 87 ..
4.22.d:
उत्पत्य च महावेगाच्चकार वेष्टनं हरेः ॥
पृथिवीं घर्षयामास तीक्ष्णाग्रेण खुरेण च ॥ 87 ॥
4.22.m:
And springing up with great speed, he encircled Hari;
he scraped the earth with his sharp-pointed hoof.

4.22.s:
pragṛhya śrīhariṃ vegātkṛtvā mūrdhni mahāsuraḥ ..
utpapāta manoyāyī līlayā lakṣayojanam .. 88 ..
4.22.d:
प्रगृह्य श्रीहरिं वेगात्कृत्वा मूर्ध्नि महासुरः ॥
उत्पपात मनोयायी लीलया लक्षयोजनम् ॥ 88 ॥
4.22.m:
Seizing Śrī Hari swiftly and placing him upon his head, the great asura,
traveling at the speed of thought, flew up easily a hundred thousand yojanas.

4.22.s:
praharaṃ ca tayoryuddhaṃ nirlakṣe ca babhūva ha ..
tato gṛhītvā śrīkṛṣṇaṃ papāta dharaṇītale .. 89 ..
4.22.d:
प्रहरं च तयोर्युद्धं निर्लक्षे च बभूव ह ॥
ततो गृहीत्वा श्रीकृष्णं पपात धरणीतले ॥ 89 ॥
4.22.m:
And their battle took place out of sight for a prahara.
Then, holding Śrī Kṛṣṇa, he fell down to the surface of the earth.

4.22.s:
punarmuhūrtaṃ yuddhaṃ ca babhūva bhūtale tayoḥ ..
mudā hariḥ praśaśaṃsa prahasya dānaveśvaram .. 4.22.90 ..
4.22.d:
पुनर्मुहूर्तं युद्धं च बभूव भूतले तयोः ॥
मुदा हरिः प्रशशंस प्रहस्य दानवेश्वरम् ॥ 4.22.90 ॥
4.22.m:
Again, a battle between the two occurred on the earth for a muhūrta.
Hari with joy praised the lord of the Dānavas, laughing gently:

4.22.s:
madbhaktasya baleḥ putraṃ dhanyaṃ tajjīvanaṃ param..
svastyastu te dānavendra vatsa nirvāṇatāṃ vraja .. 91 ..
4.22.d:
मद्भक्तस्य बलेः पुत्रं धन्यं तज्जीवनं परम्॥
स्वस्त्यस्तु ते दानवेन्द्र वत्स निर्वाणतां व्रज ॥ 91 ॥
4.22.m:
“O son of Bali, my devotee! Blessed, supremely so, is his life.
Hail to you, O lord of the Dānavas! Go, my child, to the state of nirvāṇa!

4.22.s:
maddarśanaṃ svastibījaṃ paraṃ nirvāṇakāraṇam ..
sarvādhikaṃ sarvaparaṃ labha sthānaṃ manoharam .. 92 ..
4.22.d:
मद्दर्शनं स्वस्तिबीजं परं निर्वाणकारणम् ॥
सर्वाधिकं सर्वपरं लभ स्थानं मनोहरम् ॥ 92 ॥
4.22.m:
The sight of me is the seed of auspiciousness, the supreme cause of nirvāṇa.
Attain that charming abode, superior to all, beyond all!”

4.22.s:
ityevamuktvā śrīkṛṣṇaḥ sasmāra cakramuttamam ..
sūryakoṭisamaṃ dīptyā jagrāha tatsudarśanam ..93..
4.22.d:
इत्येवमुक्त्वा श्रीकृष्णः सस्मार चक्रमुत्तमम् ॥
सूर्यकोटिसमं दीप्त्या जग्राह तत्सुदर्शनम् ॥93॥
4.22.m:
Having spoken thus, Śrī Kṛṣṇa remembered his excellent discus.
Equal to ten million suns in radiance, he took up that Sudarśana.

4.22.s:
cikṣepa bhrāmayitvā ca ṣoḍaśāramanuttamam ..
ciccheda līlayā'vadhyaṃ brahmaviṣṇumaheśvaraiḥ .. 94 ..
4.22.d:
चिक्षेप भ्रामयित्वा च षोडशारमनुत्तमम् ॥
चिच्छेद लीलयाऽवध्यं ब्रह्मविष्णुमहेश्वरैः ॥ 94 ॥
4.22.m:
And having whirled that unexcelled sixteen-spoked [discus], he hurled it;
with ease he severed him who was invulnerable to Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara.

4.22.s:
papāta mastakaṃ bhūmau dānavasya mahātmanaḥ ..
tejaḥsamūha uttasthau śatasūryasamaprabhaḥ.. 95 ..
4.22.d:
पपात मस्तकं भूमौ दानवस्य महात्मनः ॥
तेजःसमूह उत्तस्थौ शतसूर्यसमप्रभः॥ 95 ॥
4.22.m:
The head of that great-souled Dānava fell upon the earth.
A mass of splendor arose, with brilliance like a hundred suns;

4.22.s:
vilokya harilokaṃ saṃśliṣṭaṃ kṛṣṇapadāmbuje ..
saṃprāpya paramaṃ mokṣamaho dānavapuṅgavaḥ .. 96 ..
4.22.d:
विलोक्य हरिलोकं संश्लिष्टं कृष्णपदाम्बुजे ॥
संप्राप्य परमं मोक्षमहो दानवपुङ्गवः ॥ 96 ॥
4.22.m:
beholding the realm of Hari, it merged into the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa.
Ah, that foremost of Dānavas attained supreme liberation!

4.22.s:
gaganasthāḥ surāḥ sarve munayaśca bhṛśaṃ mudā ..
pārijātaprasūnānāṃ cakruste tatra varṣaṇam ..97..
4.22.d:
गगनस्थाः सुराः सर्वे मुनयश्च भृशं मुदा ॥
पारिजातप्रसूनानां चक्रुस्ते तत्र वर्षणम् ॥97॥
4.22.m:
All the gods in the sky and the sages, filled with great joy,
made a rain of pārijāta blossoms upon that spot.

4.22.s:
nedurdundubhayaḥ svarge nanṛtuścāpsarogaṇāḥ ..
jagurgandharvanikarā stuṣṭuvurmunayo mudā .. 98 ..
4.22.d:
नेदुर्दुन्दुभयः स्वर्गे ननृतुश्चाप्सरोगणाः ॥
जगुर्गन्धर्वनिकरा स्तुष्टुवुर्मुनयो मुदा ॥ 98 ॥
4.22.m:
Drums sounded in heaven, and troops of Apsarases danced;
multitudes of Gandharvas sang, and sages joyfully praised [him].

4.22.s:
stutvā jagmuḥ surāḥ sarve munayo harṣavihvalāḥ ..
dhenukasya vadhaṃ dṛṣṭvā tatrājagmuśca bālakāḥ .. 99 ..
4.22.d:
स्तुत्वा जग्मुः सुराः सर्वे मुनयो हर्षविह्वलाः ॥
धेनुकस्य वधं दृष्ट्वा तत्राजग्मुश्च बालकाः ॥ 99 ॥
4.22.m:
Having offered praise, all the gods and sages went away, overwhelmed with joy.
Seeing the slaying of Dhenuka, the boys came there.

4.22.s:
balaśca balināṃ śreṣṭhastuṣṭāva puruṣottamam ..
tuṣṭuvurbālakāḥ sarve nanṛtuśca mudā'nvitāḥ .. 4.22.100 ..
4.22.d:
बलश्च बलिनां श्रेष्ठस्तुष्टाव पुरुषोत्तमम् ॥
तुष्टुवुर्बालकाः सर्वे ननृतुश्च मुदाऽन्विताः ॥ 4.22.100 ॥
4.22.m:
And Bala, the best of the strong, praised Puruṣottama.
All the boys praised [him] and danced, filled with joy.

4.22.s:
dattvā kṛṣṇabalābhyāṃ ca prapakvāni phalāni ca ..
sarvāṇi bhakṣayāmāsurbālāḥ prahaṣṭamānasāḥ .. 101 ..
4.22.d:
दत्त्वा कृष्णबलाभ्यां च प्रपक्वानि फलानि च ॥
सर्वाणि भक्षयामासुर्बालाः प्रहष्टमानसाः ॥ 101 ॥
4.22.m:
Having offered the fully ripe fruits to Kṛṣṇa and Bala,
the boys, their minds exceedingly delighted, ate them all.

4.22.s:
bhuktvā pītvā hariḥ śīghraṃ balena bālakaiḥ saha ..
jagāma svālayaṃ brahmannihatya dānaveśvaram..102..
.. 22 ..
4.22.d:
भुक्त्वा पीत्वा हरिः शीघ्रं बलेन बालकैः सह ॥
जगाम स्वालयं ब्रह्मन्निहत्य दानवेश्वरम्॥102॥
॥ 22 ॥
4.22.m:
Having eaten and drunk, Hari quickly, together with Bala and the boys,
went to his own home, O sage, having slain the lord of the Dānavas.

4.23.s:
nārada uvāca ..
kena pāpena balijo gardabhatvamavāpa ha ..
durvāsāḥ kena doṣeṇa śaśāpa dānaveśvaram .. 1 ..
4.23.d:
नारद उवाच ॥
केन पापेन बलिजो गर्दभत्वमवाप ह ॥
दुर्वासाः केन दोषेण शशाप दानवेश्वरम् ॥ 1 ॥
4.23.m:
Nārada said:
“By what sin did the son of Bali attain the form of an ass?
For what fault did Durvāsas curse the lord of the Dānavas? / 1
Or by what merit, O Lord, did that mighty chief of the Dānavas
attain the abode of Śrī Hari and immediate liberation of oneness? / 2
O sage, dispel my doubts and tell everything in full detail.
Ah, in the mouth of a poet, poetry is ever fresh at every step!” / 3
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:
“Listen, my child, I shall narrate the ancient history
formerly heard from the mouth of Dharma on Mount Gandhamādana, / 4
an account from the Pādma kalpa, wondrous and very charming,
imbued with tales of Nārāyaṇa, supreme nectar to the ears. / 5
In the kalpa wherein this tale occurred, you were Upabarhaṇa,
living for an entire kalpa, glorious, handsome, endowed with perpetual youth, / 6
the husband of fifty passionate women, intent on amorous delights;
and by a boon from Brahmā, you had a sweet voice, a master of singers. / 7
Incessantly, those women drank in your handsome lotus-face,
all of them never blinking, tormented by the arrows of love. / 8
You were, as it were, fashioned by the Creator out of their life-breaths, so it is heard;
as your companions day and night, they could not live without you. / 9
In flower gardens and in secret, in charming place after place,
in the caves of mountains, in chasms and by rivers, / 10
in delightful forests and in graveyards devoid of living beings,
they engaged in amorous play with you according to their desire. / 11
Then, by fate and through a curse of the Creator, you became the son of a maidservant;
now you are the son of Brahmā, due to eating the remnants of a Vaiṣṇava's food, / 12
living for countless kalpas, a great and foremost Vaiṣṇava,
all-seeing through the vision of knowledge, and a dear disciple of Dhūrjaṭi. / 13
O sage, hear from me the account of that kalpa;
I shall tell you at length the nectar-like story of the Daitya. / 14
Once, indeed, the mighty son of Bali, named Sāhasika…”

4.23.s:
kena puṇyena vā nātha balinaḥ śrīhareḥ padam ..
sahasaikatvamuktiṃ ca saṃprāpa dānavādhipaḥ .. 2 ..
4.23.d:
केन पुण्येन वा नाथ बलिनः श्रीहरेः पदम् ॥
सहसैकत्वमुक्तिं च संप्राप दानवाधिपः ॥ 2 ॥

4.23.s:
mune sarvaṃ suvistārya vada saṃdehabhañjana ..
aho kavimukhe kāvyaṃ nūtnaṃnūtnaṃ padepade .. 3 ..
4.23.d:
मुने सर्वं सुविस्तार्य वद संदेहभञ्जन ॥
अहो कविमुखे काव्यं नूत्नंनूत्नं पदेपदे ॥ 3 ॥

4.23.s:
śrīnārāyaṇa uvāca ..
śṛṇu vatsa pravakṣye'hamitihāsaṃ purātanam ..
purā śrutaṃ dharmavaktrātparvate gandhamādane .. 4 ..
4.23.d:
श्रीनारायण उवाच ॥
शृणु वत्स प्रवक्ष्येऽहमितिहासं पुरातनम् ॥
पुरा श्रुतं धर्मवक्त्रात्पर्वते गन्धमादने ॥ 4 ॥

4.23.s:
pādmakalpe ca vṛttāntaṃ vicitraṃ sumanoharam ..
nārāyaṇakathopetaṃ karṇapīyūṣamuttamam .. 5 ..
4.23.d:
पाद्मकल्पे च वृत्तान्तं विचित्रं सुमनोहरम् ॥
नारायणकथोपेतं कर्णपीयूषमुत्तमम् ॥ 5 ॥

4.23.s:
yatra kalpe kathā ceyaṃ tatra tvamupabarhaṇaḥ ..
ākalpajīvī saśrīkaḥ sundaraḥ sthirayauvanaḥ .. 6 ..
4.23.d:
यत्र कल्पे कथा चेयं तत्र त्वमुपबर्हणः ॥
आकल्पजीवी सश्रीकः सुन्दरः स्थिरयौवनः ॥ 6 ॥
4.23.m: In that kalpa where this story took place, you were Upabarhaṇa,

4.23.s:
paṃcāśatkāminīnāṃ ca patiḥ śṛṅgāratatparaḥ ..
vareṇa brahmaṇastvaṃ ca sukaṇṭho gāyaneśvaraḥ .. 7 ..
4.23.d:
पंचाशत्कामिनीनां च पतिः शृङ्गारतत्परः ॥
वरेण ब्रह्मणस्त्वं च सुकण्ठो गायनेश्वरः ॥ 7 ॥

4.23.s:
anukṣaṇaṃ papustāste sundaraṃ mukhapaṅkajam ..
nimeṣarahitāḥ sarvāḥ kāmabāṇaprapīḍitāḥ .. 8 ..
4.23.d:
अनुक्षणं पपुस्तास्ते सुन्दरं मुखपङ्कजम् ॥
निमेषरहिताः सर्वाः कामबाणप्रपीडिताः ॥ 8 ॥

4.23.s:
tāsāṃ prāṇaiśca ghaṭito vidhinā tvamiva śrutam ..
divāniśaṃ sahacarā na jīvanti tvayā vinā ..
.. 9 .. puṣpodyāne ca rahasi sthānesthāne manorame ..
4.23.d:
तासां प्राणैश्च घटितो विधिना त्वमिव श्रुतम् ॥
दिवानिशं सहचरा न जीवन्ति त्वया विना ॥
॥ 9 ॥ पुष्पोद्याने च रहसि स्थानेस्थाने मनोरमे ॥

4.23.s: gahvareṣu ca śailānāṃ kandareṣu nadīṣu ca .. 4.23.10 ..
4.23.d: गह्वरेषु च शैलानां कन्दरेषु नदीषु च ॥ 4.23.10 ॥

4.23.s:
kānaneṣu ca ramyeṣu śmaśāne jantuvarjite ..
yathāmanorathaṃ tāśca krīḍāṃ cakrustvayā saha .. 11 ..
4.23.d:
काननेषु च रम्येषु श्मशाने जन्तुवर्जिते ॥
यथामनोरथं ताश्च क्रीडां चक्रुस्त्वया सह ॥ 11 ॥

4.23.s:
tadā daivādvidheḥ śāpādbhūtvā dāsīsuto bhavān ..
adhunā brahmaṇaḥ putro vaiṣṇavocchiṣṭabhojanāt .. 12 ..
4.23.d:
तदा दैवाद्विधेः शापाद्भूत्वा दासीसुतो भवान् ॥
अधुना ब्रह्मणः पुत्रो वैष्णवोच्छिष्टभोजनात् ॥ 12 ॥

4.23.s:
asaṃkhyakalpajīvī ca vaiṣṇavapravaro mahān ..
jñānadṛṣṭyā sarvadarśī priya śiṣyaśca dhūrjaṭeḥ .. 13 ..
4.23.d:
असंख्यकल्पजीवी च वैष्णवप्रवरो महान् ॥
ज्ञानदृष्ट्या सर्वदर्शी प्रिय शिष्यश्च धूर्जटेः ॥ 13 ॥

4.23.s:
tasya kalpasya vṛttāntaṃ mune matto niśāmaya ..
vistārya daityavṛttāṃtaṃ kathayāmi sudhopamam ..14..
4.23.d:
तस्य कल्पस्य वृत्तान्तं मुने मत्तो निशामय ॥
विस्तार्य दैत्यवृत्तांतं कथयामि सुधोपमम् ॥14॥

4.23.s:
ekadaiva baleḥ putro nāmnā sāhasiko balī ..
svatejasā surāñjitvā pratasthe gandhamādanam .. 19 ..
4.23.d:
एकदैव बलेः पुत्रो नाम्ना साहसिको बली ॥
स्वतेजसा सुराञ्जित्वा प्रतस्थे गन्धमादनम् ॥ 19 ॥

4.23.s:
candenokṣitasarvāṅgo ratnabhūṣaṇabhūṣitaḥ ..
ratnasiṃhāsanasthaśca bahusainyasamanvitaḥ .. 16 ..
4.23.d:
चन्देनोक्षितसर्वाङ्गो रत्नभूषणभूषितः ॥
रत्नसिंहासनस्थश्च बहुसैन्यसमन्वितः ॥ 16 ॥

4.23.s:
etasminnantare tena pathā yāti tilottamā ..
rūpeṇāpsarasāṃ śreṣṭhā nānāveṣavidhāyinī .. 17 ..
4.23.d:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे तेन पथा याति तिलोत्तमा ॥
रूपेणाप्सरसां श्रेष्ठा नानावेषविधायिनी ॥ 17 ॥

4.23.s:
cārucampakavarṇābhā ratnābharaṇabhūṣitā ..
navayauvanasampannā kāmabāṇaprapīḍitā .. 18 ..
4.23.d:
चारुचम्पकवर्णाभा रत्नाभरणभूषिता ॥
नवयौवनसम्पन्ना कामबाणप्रपीडिता ॥ 18 ॥

4.23.s:
īṣaddhāsya prasannāsyā divyavastraṃ subibhratī ..
vakrabhūbhaṅgayuktā sā gajendramandagāminī .. 19 ..
4.23.d:
ईषद्धास्य प्रसन्नास्या दिव्यवस्त्रं सुबिभ्रती ॥
वक्रभूभङ्गयुक्ता सा गजेन्द्रमन्दगामिनी ॥ 19 ॥

4.23.s:
stanamūruṃ mukhenduṃ ca dṛṣṭvā sāhasiko yuvā ..
vāyunā muktavastrāyāstasyā mūrcchāmavāpa ha .. 4.23.20 ..
4.23.d:
स्तनमूरुं मुखेन्दुं च दृष्ट्वा साहसिको युवा ॥
वायुना मुक्तवस्त्रायास्तस्या मूर्च्छामवाप ह ॥ 4.23.20 ॥

4.23.s:
sā dadarśa baleḥ putramatīva sumanoharam ..
praphullamālatīmālāṃ bibhrataṃ navayauvanam .. 21 ..
4.23.d:
सा ददर्श बलेः पुत्रमतीव सुमनोहरम् ॥
प्रफुल्लमालतीमालां बिभ्रतं नवयौवनम् ॥ 21 ॥

4.23.s:
śaratpārvaṇacandrāsyaṃ susmitaṃ sumanoharam ..
dṛṣṭvā taṃ vismitā kāmātkaṭākṣaṃ ca cakāra sā .. 22 ..
4.23.d:
शरत्पार्वणचन्द्रास्यं सुस्मितं सुमनोहरम् ॥
दृष्ट्वा तं विस्मिता कामात्कटाक्षं च चकार सा ॥ 22 ॥

4.23.s:
krīḍāyai candralokaṃ ca gacchantī candrakāmukī ..
tasthau kena cchalenaiva mattā śṛṅgāralālasā .. 23 ..
4.23.d:
क्रीडायै चन्द्रलोकं च गच्छन्ती चन्द्रकामुकी ॥
तस्थौ केन च्छलेनैव मत्ता शृङ्गारलालसा ॥ 23 ॥

4.23.s:
darśaṃdarśaṃ ca tasyāsya prahasya vakracakṣuṣā ..
mukhasyācchādanaṃ cakre vāsasā sā punaḥpunaḥ .. 24 ..
4.23.d:
दर्शंदर्शं च तस्यास्य प्रहस्य वक्रचक्षुषा ॥
मुखस्याच्छादनं चक्रे वाससा सा पुनःपुनः ॥ 24 ॥

4.23.s:
pulakāṃkitasarvāṅgaṃ dharmakarmasamanvitam ..
babhūva kāmamattāyā yonau kaṇḍūyanaṃ jalam .. 25 ..
4.23.d:
पुलकांकितसर्वाङ्गं धर्मकर्मसमन्वितम् ॥
बभूव काममत्ताया योनौ कण्डूयनं जलम् ॥ 25 ॥

4.23.s:
visasmāra śaśadharaṃ baliputramanorathā ..
aho ko veda bhuvane durjñeyaṃ puṃścalīmanaḥ .. 26 ..
4.23.d:
विसस्मार शशधरं बलिपुत्रमनोरथा ॥
अहो को वेद भुवने दुर्ज्ञेयं पुंश्चलीमनः ॥ 26 ॥

4.23.s:
puṃścalyāṃ yo hi viśvasto vidhinā sa viḍambitaḥ ..
bahiṣkṛtaśca yaśasā dharmeṇa svakulena ca..27..
4.23.d:
पुंश्चल्यां यो हि विश्वस्तो विधिना स विडम्बितः ॥
बहिष्कृतश्च यशसा धर्मेण स्वकुलेन च॥27॥

4.23.s:
vāñchitaṃ nūtanaṃ prāpya vinaśyati purātanam ..
tadā svakarmasādhyā sā ko vā tasyāḥ priyo'priyaḥ ..28..
4.23.d:
वाञ्छितं नूतनं प्राप्य विनश्यति पुरातनम् ॥
तदा स्वकर्मसाध्या सा को वा तस्याः प्रियोऽप्रियः ॥28॥

4.23.s:
daive karmaṇi paitrye ca putre bandhau na bhartari ..
dāruṇaṃ puṃścalīcittaṃ sadā śṛṅgārakarmaṇi .. 29 ..
4.23.d:
दैवे कर्मणि पैत्र्ये च पुत्रे बन्धौ न भर्तरि ॥
दारुणं पुंश्चलीचित्तं सदा शृङ्गारकर्मणि ॥ 29 ॥
4.23.m: Having conquered the gods with his own splendor, he set out for Mount Gandhamādana. / His entire body was anointed with sandal-paste, and he was adorned with jeweled ornaments. / Seated on a jeweled throne, he was accompanied by a vast army. / Meanwhile, along that path went Tilottamā, / the best of apsarases in beauty, assuming various attire. / She had the lovely complexion of a campaka flower, was adorned with jeweled ornaments, / endowed with fresh youth, and afflicted by the arrows of Kāma. / With a gentle smile and a serene face, wearing splendid divine garments, / she walked with curved brows, moving slowly like a noble elephant. / Seeing her breasts, thighs, and moon-like face as her garment was displaced by the wind, the daring young man fell into a swoon. / She beheld the son of Bali, exceedingly handsome, / wearing a garland of blooming mālatī flowers, in his fresh youth, / with a face like the full moon of autumn, smiling sweetly and charming the mind. / Seeing him, she was astonished and, out of passion, cast a sidelong glance. / Going to the realm of Candra for sport, desiring Candra, / she stopped under some pretext, intoxicated and longing for erotic pleasure. / Constantly looking at his face and laughing with curved glances, / she covered her face again and again with her garment. / Her entire body bristled with thrill; though endowed with righteous deeds, / being mad with lust, there arose itching and moisture in her yoni. / Yearning for Bali's son, she forgot the moon. / Ah, who in the world knows the unsearchable mind of an unchaste woman? / He who trusts an unchaste woman is mocked by fate, / and is cast out from fame, from righteousness, and from his own family. / Having obtained a new object of desire, the old one perishes; / then, guided only by her own purpose, who is dear or not dear to her? / In religious rites for the gods, in rites for the ancestors, towards a son, a kinsman, or a husband— / an unchaste woman's heart is cruel, always fixed on the act of love.

4.23.s:
prāṇādhikaṃ ratijñaṃ sā'mṛtadṛṣṭyā ca puṃścalī ..
ratnapradaṃ ratnavijñaṃ viṣadṛṣṭyā hi paśyati .. 4.23.30 ..
4.23.d:
प्राणाधिकं रतिज्ञं साऽमृतदृष्ट्या च पुंश्चली ॥
रत्नप्रदं रत्नविज्ञं विषदृष्ट्या हि पश्यति ॥ 4.23.30 ॥
4.23.m: With an affectionate gaze, the unchaste woman looks upon one skilled in lovemaking who is dearer to her than life; / but with a venomous look she regards one who gives jewels and knows the value of jewels. / For all others there is a place, but for unchaste women there is none anywhere; / the race of unchaste women is even more terrible than murderers of men. / At the end of experiencing the fruits of all deeds, there is certainly deliverance for everyone; / but for unchaste women, O best of brahmins, there is none as long as the moon and the sun endure. / The pity that other women have even toward killing an insect / does not exist in unchaste women: she kills her former lover. / Seeing her former lover, she certainly destroys him easily by some contrivance; / having obtained a new man skilled in love, the old one becomes like poison to her. / Whatever sins exist on earth among unchaste women in Bhārata, / there are no greater sinners than them. / Food cooked by an unchaste woman is certain to contain all sins; / in rites for the gods and for the ancestors, even water from her must not be offered. / The food of unchaste women is certainly feces, and their water is urine; / having offered it to the ancestors and the gods, and having eaten it, one goes to hell. / In the most terrible Kālasūtra he bakes for a hundred years; / in dreadful darkness worms bite him day and night. / If by chance the lowest of men eats the food of an unchaste woman, / his merit acquired over seven births is certainly destroyed. / There is a loss of lifespan, fortune, and fame in this world and the next; / therefore, with great effort one must guard one's cooking pot and wife. / In merely seeing an unchaste woman there is merit, and success of a journey is certain; / but in touching her there is a great sin, from which one is purified by bathing in holy waters. / Bathing, giving gifts, vows, chanting, and worship of deities / are fruitless for unchaste people; their life in Bhārata is in vain. / Thus the account of the unchaste woman, hard to comprehend, has been told according to tradition. / Now hear the actual conversation between the two there, O Nārada.

4.23.s:
sarveṣāṃ sthalamastyeva puṃścalīnāṃ na kutracit ..
dāruṇā puṃścalī jātirnaraghātibhya eva ca ..31..
4.23.d:
सर्वेषां स्थलमस्त्येव पुंश्चलीनां न कुत्रचित् ॥
दारुणा पुंश्चली जातिर्नरघातिभ्य एव च ॥31॥

4.23.s:
niṣkṛtiḥ sarvabhogānte sarveṣāmasti niścitam..
na puṃścalīnāṃ viprendra yāvaccandradivākarau .. 32 ..
4.23.d:
निष्कृतिः सर्वभोगान्ते सर्वेषामस्ति निश्चितम्॥
न पुंश्चलीनां विप्रेन्द्र यावच्चन्द्रदिवाकरौ ॥ 32 ॥

4.23.s:
anyāsāṃ kāminīnāṃ ca kīṭaṃ hantuṃ ca yā dayā ..
sā nāsti puṃścalīnāṃ tu kāntaṃ hanti purātanam .. 33 ..
4.23.d:
अन्यासां कामिनीनां च कीटं हन्तुं च या दया ॥
सा नास्ति पुंश्चलीनां तु कान्तं हन्ति पुरातनम् ॥ 33 ॥

4.23.s:
kāntaṃ dṛṣṭvā hinastyeva sopāyenāvalīlayā ..
ratijñaṃ nūtanaṃ prāpya viṣatulyaṃ purātanam .. 34 ..
4.23.d:
कान्तं दृष्ट्वा हिनस्त्येव सोपायेनावलीलया ॥
रतिज्ञं नूतनं प्राप्य विषतुल्यं पुरातनम् ॥ 34 ॥

4.23.s:
pṛthivyāṃ yāni pāpāni puṃścalīṣveva bhārate ..
tiṣṭhanti tābhyo na parāḥ pāpiṣṭhāḥ santi kecana .. 39 ..
4.23.d:
पृथिव्यां यानि पापानि पुंश्चलीष्वेव भारते ॥
तिष्ठन्ति ताभ्यो न पराः पापिष्ठाः सन्ति केचन ॥ 39 ॥

4.23.s:
puṃścalīparipakvānnaṃ sarvapātakaniścitam ..
daive karmaṇi paitrye ca na deyaṃ ca tathā jalam .. 36 ..
4.23.d:
पुंश्चलीपरिपक्वान्नं सर्वपातकनिश्चितम् ॥
दैवे कर्मणि पैत्र्ये च न देयं च तथा जलम् ॥ 36 ॥

4.23.s:
annaṃ viṣṭhā jalaṃ mūtraṃ puṃścalīnāṃ ca niścitam ..
dattvā pitṛbhyo devebhyo bhuktvā ca narakaṃ vrajet ..37..
4.23.d:
अन्नं विष्ठा जलं मूत्रं पुंश्चलीनां च निश्चितम् ॥
दत्त्वा पितृभ्यो देवेभ्यो भुक्त्वा च नरकं व्रजेत् ॥37॥

4.23.s:
śatavarṣaṃ kālasūtre pacatyeva sudāruṇe ..
ghorāndhakāre kṛmayastaṃ daśanti divāniśam.... 38 ..
4.23.d:
शतवर्षं कालसूत्रे पचत्येव सुदारुणे ॥
घोरान्धकारे कृमयस्तं दशन्ति दिवानिशम्॥॥ 38 ॥

4.23.s:
puṃścalyannaṃ ca yo bhuṅkte daivādyadi narādhamaḥ ..
saptajanmakṛtaṃ puṇyaṃ tasya naśyati niścitam .. 39 ..
4.23.d:
पुंश्चल्यन्नं च यो भुङ्क्ते दैवाद्यदि नराधमः ॥
सप्तजन्मकृतं पुण्यं तस्य नश्यति निश्चितम् ॥ 39 ॥

4.23.s:
āyuḥ śrīyaśasāṃ hāniriha loke paratra ca ..
tasmādyatnādrakṣaṇīyaṃ pākapātraṃ kalatrakam .. 4.23.40 ..
4.23.d:
आयुः श्रीयशसां हानिरिह लोके परत्र च ॥
तस्माद्यत्नाद्रक्षणीयं पाकपात्रं कलत्रकम् ॥ 4.23.40 ॥

4.23.s:
puṃścalīdarśane puṇyaṃ yātrāsiddhirbhaveddhruvam ..
sparśane ca mahāpāpaṃ tīrthasnānādviśudhyati .. 41 ..
4.23.d:
पुंश्चलीदर्शने पुण्यं यात्रासिद्धिर्भवेद्ध्रुवम् ॥
स्पर्शने च महापापं तीर्थस्नानाद्विशुध्यति ॥ 41 ॥

4.23.s:
snānaṃ dānaṃ vrataṃ caiva japaśca devapūjanam ..
niṣphalaṃ puṃścalināṃ ca bhārate jīvanaṃ vṛthā .... 42 ..
4.23.d:
स्नानं दानं व्रतं चैव जपश्च देवपूजनम् ॥
निष्फलं पुंश्चलिनां च भारते जीवनं वृथा ॥॥ 42 ॥

4.23.s:
kathitaṃ kulaṭākhyānaṃ durjñeyaṃ ca yathāgamam ..
saṃvādaṃ ca tayostatra prakṛtaṃ śṛṇu nārada .. 43 ..
4.23.d:
कथितं कुलटाख्यानं दुर्ज्ञेयं च यथागमम् ॥
संवादं च तयोस्तत्र प्रकृतं शृणु नारद ॥ 43 ॥

4.23.s:
sa punaścetanāṃ prāpya tāṃ dṛṣṭvaiva baleḥ sutaḥ ..
kāmāturaḥ pramattaśca jagāma kulaṭāntikam .. 44 ..
4.23.d:
स पुनश्चेतनां प्राप्य तां दृष्ट्वैव बलेः सुतः ॥
कामातुरः प्रमत्तश्च जगाम कुलटान्तिकम् ॥ 44 ॥
4.23.m: Having regained consciousness and upon seeing her, the son of Bali, / distressed with passion and intoxicated with desire, approached the wanton woman. / He spoke to her of crooked side-glances, heavy hips, and plump breasts, / as she bashfully and joyfully covered her face with her garment. / Sāhasika said: / 'Who are you, whose daughter are you, whose beloved are you, O lovely lady? / Where are you going on your own, O fair-browed one? To which handsome, meritorious man / who, purified by austerity at the end of an eon, is destined to enjoy only you, O beautiful one? / Whomever you are going to, go; but you ought to make me your servant. / Purchase me, a servant greedy for lovemaking, with the merit of erotic pleasure; / you are longing for lovemaking, so grant me lovemaking, O passionate woman! / My embrace with you was ordained by destiny; / what has been determined by destiny, by whom can that be averted, O dear one? / Speak words like nectar with a smile, O beautiful woman; / quickly bind me in solitude with the cords of your creeper-like arms! / Offer an seat, O auspicious lady—your thigh resembling gold; / and display the jar-like orb of your breast, fit for a vessel! / Pierce me deeply, O passionate woman, with the sharp weapon of your sidelong glance; / heal my wound caused by the serpent of Kāma with the touch of your foot! / Give the delicious nectar of your lower lip to me, who am hungry; / show your lovely teeth that shine like seeds of a ripe pomegranate!

4.23.s:
uvāca kuṭilāpāṅgī pīnaśroṇipayodharām ..

strīṇāṃ satpuruṣāśleṣa ājīvaṃ manasi sthitaḥ .. 119 ..
4.23.d:
मां विस्मरसि कालेन पुरुषः षट्पदो यथा ॥
स्त्रीणां सत्पुरुषाश्लेष आजीवं मनसि स्थितः ॥ 119 ॥
4.23.m:
In time you will forget me, as a man [does], or a bee [with a flower].
For women, the embrace of a good man remains in the heart for life. 119

4.23.s:
satsaṃgamaḥ śubhadine puṇyātpuṇyavatāṃ bhavet ..
sadvicchedo duḥkhaheturmaraṇādatiricyate ..4.23.120..
4.23.d:
सत्संगमः शुभदिने पुण्यात्पुण्यवतां भवेत् ॥
सद्विच्छेदो दुःखहेतुर्मरणादतिरिच्यते ॥4.23.120॥
4.23.m:
Union with the virtuous occurs on an auspicious day to the meritorious from their merit;
separation from the virtuous, a cause of grief, is worse than death. 120

4.23.s:
pīyūṣabhojanātsvargavāsādapi ca durlabhaḥ ..
satsaṃgamaḥ sukhamayo'pyasatsaṅgo viṣādhikaḥ .. 121 ..
4.23.d:
पीयूषभोजनात्स्वर्गवासादपि च दुर्लभः ॥
सत्संगमः सुखमयोऽप्यसत्सङ्गो विषाधिकः ॥ 121 ॥
4.23.m:
More rare than feasting on nectar, and even than dwelling in heaven,
is delightful union with the good; but the company of the wicked is worse than poison. 121

4.23.s:
kṣaṇaṃ tiṣṭha mahārāja punarāliṃganaṃ kuru ..
tvayā sārdhaṃ mama prāṇā yāsyanti cetasā saha ..122..
4.23.d:
क्षणं तिष्ठ महाराज पुनरालिंगनं कुरु ॥
त्वया सार्धं मम प्राणा यास्यन्ति चेतसा सह ॥122॥
4.23.m:
Stay for a moment, great king! Embrace me again!
Along with you, my life-breaths will depart, together with my mind. 122

4.23.s:
ityevamuktvā kulaṭā kṛtvā vakṣasi sādaram ..
pumaṃgasaṃgotpulakā mūrcchāmāpa sukhena ca .. 123 ..
4.23.d:
इत्येवमुक्त्वा कुलटा कृत्वा वक्षसि सादरम् ॥
पुमंगसंगोत्पुलका मूर्च्छामाप सुखेन च ॥ 123 ॥
4.23.m:
Having spoken thus, the wanton woman affectionately held him to her chest;
her hair standing on end from contact with the man's body, she fainted with pleasure. 123

4.23.s:
kulaṭāliṃganālāpātso'tikāmī babhūva ha ..
yathā dīptaḥ kṛṣṇavartmā vardhate haviṣā'dhikam .. 124 ..
4.23.d:
कुलटालिंगनालापात्सोऽतिकामी बभूव ह ॥
यथा दीप्तः कृष्णवर्त्मा वर्धते हविषाऽधिकम् ॥ 124 ॥
4.23.m:
From the unchaste woman's embrace and talk, he became intensely lustful,
just as a blazing fire flares up all the more with ghee. 124

4.23.s:
punaścakāra śṛṃgāramasuro'ṣṭavidhaṃ mune ..
cuṃbanaṃ ca navavidhaṃ yathāsthāne yathocitam .. 125 ..
4.23.d:
पुनश्चकार शृंगारमसुरोऽष्टविधं मुने ॥
चुंबनं च नवविधं यथास्थाने यथोचितम् ॥ 125 ॥
4.23.m:
Again the Asura made eightfold love, O sage,
and gave the nine kinds of kisses in the proper places, as was fitting. 125

4.23.s:
nakhadantakaraiḥ krīḍāṃ cakāra vividhāṃ punaḥ ..
kiṃkiṇīnāṃ kaṃkaṇānāṃ babhūva śabda ulbaṇaḥ ..
munerdurvāsasastena dhyānabhaṅgo babhūva ha .. 126 ..
4.23.d:
नखदन्तकरैः क्रीडां चकार विविधां पुनः ॥
किंकिणीनां कंकणानां बभूव शब्द उल्बणः ॥
मुनेर्दुर्वाससस्तेन ध्यानभङ्गो बभूव ह ॥ 126 ॥
4.23.m:
He played varied games again with fingernails, teeth, and hands.
There arose a loud sound from waist-bells and bracelets,
and because of that, the meditation of sage Durvāsas was broken. 126

4.23.s:
adṛṣṭasya tayostatra valmīkācchāditasya ca ..
yogāsanaṃ kurvataśca gandhamādanagahvare .. 127 ..
4.23.d:
अदृष्टस्य तयोस्तत्र वल्मीकाच्छादितस्य च ॥
योगासनं कुर्वतश्च गन्धमादनगह्वरे ॥ 127 ॥
4.23.m:
He was unseen by the two of them there, covered by an anthill,
practising a yogic posture in a cave of Mount Gandhamādana, 127

4.23.s:
dhyāyataścaraṇāṃbhojaṃ kṛṣṇasya paramātmanaḥ ..
na papāta tayordṛṣṭiḥ samīpasthe mahāmunau ..
kāmātmanorna hi jñānaṃ kāmena hatacetasoḥ .. 128 ..
4.23.d:
ध्यायतश्चरणांभोजं कृष्णस्य परमात्मनः ॥
न पपात तयोर्दृष्टिः समीपस्थे महामुनौ ॥
कामात्मनोर्न हि ज्ञानं कामेन हतचेतसोः ॥ 128 ॥

4.23.s:
sahasā cetanāṃ prāpya prajvalanbrahmatejasā ..
dadarśa puratastau tu munirunmīlya locane .. 129 ..
4.23.d:
सहसा चेतनां प्राप्य प्रज्वलन्ब्रह्मतेजसा ॥
ददर्श पुरतस्तौ तु मुनिरुन्मील्य लोचने ॥ 129 ॥
4.23.m:
Suddenly regaining consciousness, blazing with the splendour of Brahman,
the sage opened his eyes and saw the two before him. 129

4.23.s:
divāniśaṃ na jānantau saṃyuktau kāmamohitau ..
dṛṣṭvā cukopa tejasvī rudrāṃśo bhagavānvibhuḥ .. 4.23.130 ..
4.23.d:
दिवानिशं न जानन्तौ संयुक्तौ काममोहितौ ॥
दृष्ट्वा चुकोप तेजस्वी रुद्रांशो भगवान्विभुः ॥ 4.23.130 ॥
4.23.m:
Knowing neither day nor night, united, bewitched by passion,
seeing them, the splendid, all-pervading lord, a portion of Rudra, became enraged. 130

4.23.s:
uvāca tau vihārānte raktapaṅkajalocanaḥ ..
dhyānaprāptapadāmbhojavicchedodvignamānasaḥ .. 131 ..
4.23.d:
उवाच तौ विहारान्ते रक्तपङ्कजलोचनः ॥
ध्यानप्राप्तपदाम्भोजविच्छेदोद्विग्नमानसः ॥ 131 ॥
4.23.m:
His eyes like red lotuses, at the end of their dalliance he spoke to them,
his mind agitated at being severed from the lotus feet attained in meditation. 131

4.23.s:
durvāsā uvāca ..
uttiṣṭha gardabhākāra nirlajja puruṣādhama ..
bhaktapradhānasya baleḥ putraḥ paśusamaprabhaḥ .. 132 ..
4.23.d:
दुर्वासा उवाच ॥
उत्तिष्ठ गर्दभाकार निर्लज्ज पुरुषाधम ॥
भक्तप्रधानस्य बलेः पुत्रः पशुसमप्रभः ॥ 132 ॥
4.23.m:
Get up, you donkey-like, shameless, vilest of men!
A son of Bali, the chief of devotees, yet possessing the nature of a beast! 132

4.23.s:
devo vā mānavo vā'pi daityagandharvarākṣasāḥ ..
lajjāṃ kurvanti satataṃ svajātau ca paśūnvinā .. 133 ..
4.23.d:
देवो वा मानवो वाऽपि दैत्यगन्धर्वराक्षसाः ॥
लज्जां कुर्वन्ति सततं स्वजातौ च पशून्विना ॥ 133 ॥
4.23.m:
Whether gods or mortals, Daityas, Gandharvas, or Rākṣasas,
all show shame within their own kind, except for beasts; 133

4.23.s:
jñānalajjāvihīnā ca kharajātirviśeṣataḥ ..
tasmāttvaṃ dānavaśreṣṭha kharayoniṃ vrajādhunā .. 134 ..
4.23.d:
ज्ञानलज्जाविहीना च खरजातिर्विशेषतः ॥
तस्मात्त्वं दानवश्रेष्ठ खरयोनिं व्रजाधुना ॥ 134 ॥
4.23.m:
and the species of donkeys is especially devoid of sense and shame.
Therefore, best of Dānavas, go now into the womb of a donkey! 134

4.23.s:
tilottame tvamuttiṣṭha lajjāhīnā ca puṃścalī ..
etādṛśī spṛhā daitye vraja yoniṃ ca dānavīm .. 135 ..
4.23.d:
तिलोत्तमे त्वमुत्तिष्ठ लज्जाहीना च पुंश्चली ॥
एतादृशी स्पृहा दैत्ये व्रज योनिं च दानवीम् ॥ 135 ॥
4.23.m:
You too, Tilottamā, get up, shameless harlot!
Since you have such longing for a Daitya, go into the womb of a Dānava woman! 135

4.23.s:
ityevamuktvā sa munistasthau tatra ruṣā
jvalan .. tau ca tuṣṭuvaturbhītāvutthāya vrīḍitau munima .. 136 ..
4.23.d:
इत्येवमुक्त्वा स मुनिस्तस्थौ तत्र रुषा
ज्वलन् ॥ तौ च तुष्टुवतुर्भीतावुत्थाय व्रीडितौ मुनिम ॥ 136 ॥
4.23.m: Having spoken thus, the sage stood there blazing with wrath; / and the two of them, terrified and ashamed, arose and praised the sage. 136

4.23.s:
sāhasika uvāca ..
tvaṃ brahmā tvaṃ ca viṣṇuśca tvaṃ ca sākṣānmaheśvaraḥ ..
hutāśanastvaṃ sūryaśca sṛṣṭisthityantakārakaḥ ..137..
4.23.d:
साहसिक उवाच ॥
त्वं ब्रह्मा त्वं च विष्णुश्च त्वं च साक्षान्महेश्वरः ॥
हुताशनस्त्वं सूर्यश्च सृष्टिस्थित्यन्तकारकः ॥137॥
4.23.m:
You are Brahmā, you are Viṣṇu, and you are Maheśvara in person.
You are the Fire, and the Sun, the maker of creation, preservation, and dissolution. 137

4.23.s:
kṣamāparādhaṃ bhagavankṛpāṃ kuru kṛpānidhe ..
mūḍhāparādhaṃ satataṃ yaḥ kṣametsa sadīśvaraḥ .. 138 ..
4.23.d:
क्षमापराधं भगवन्कृपां कुरु कृपानिधे ॥
मूढापराधं सततं यः क्षमेत्स सदीश्वरः ॥ 138 ॥
4.23.m:
Forgive my offence, O Lord! Have mercy, O treasure of mercy!
He who continually forgives the offence of the foolish is truly the Lord. 138

4.23.s:
ityevamuktvā daityendro rurodoccaiḥ puro muneḥ ..
kṛtvā tṛṇāni daśane papāta caraṇāmbuje .. 139 ..
4.23.d:
इत्येवमुक्त्वा दैत्येन्द्रो रुरोदोच्चैः पुरो मुनेः ॥
कृत्वा तृणानि दशने पपात चरणाम्बुजे ॥ 139 ॥
4.23.m:
Having spoken thus, the lord of Daityas wept loudly before the sage;
placing blades of grass between his teeth, he fell at his lotus feet. 139

4.23.s:
tilottamovāca ..
he nātha karuṇāsindho dīnabandho kṛpāṃ kuru ..
vidhisṛṣṭau ca sarveṣāṃ mūḍhā strījātireva ca .. 4.23.140 ..
4.23.d:
तिलोत्तमोवाच ॥
हे नाथ करुणासिन्धो दीनबन्धो कृपां कुरु ॥
विधिसृष्टौ च सर्वेषां मूढा स्त्रीजातिरेव च ॥ 4.23.140 ॥
4.23.m: Among all the creation of the Creator, womankind is indeed foolish; 140

4.23.s:
tato'timattā kulaṭā sadā kāmāturā parā ..
lajjābhītiścetanā ca na santi kāmuke vibho .. 141 ..
4.23.d:
ततोऽतिमत्ता कुलटा सदा कामातुरा परा ॥
लज्जाभीतिश्चेतना च न सन्ति कामुके विभो ॥ 141 ॥
4.23.m:
and beyond that, a wanton woman is utterly intoxicated, constantly stricken with lust.
Shame, fear, and consciousness do not exist in one who is lustful, O lord. 141

4.23.s:
ityuktvā rodanaṃ kṛtvā jagāma śaraṇaṃ muneḥ ..
vinā vipattau keṣāṃcijjñānaṃ bhavati bhūtale ..
tayordṛṣṭvā ca vaikalyaṃ babhūva karuṇā muneḥ .. 142 ..
4.23.d:
इत्युक्त्वा रोदनं कृत्वा जगाम शरणं मुनेः ॥
विना विपत्तौ केषांचिज्ज्ञानं भवति भूतले ॥
तयोर्दृष्ट्वा च वैकल्यं बभूव करुणा मुनेः ॥ 142 ॥

4.23.s:
durvāsā uvāca ..
atiśāpaḥ prasādo vā bhaveddaivena dānava ..
satkīrtirapakīrtirvā prāktanaprabhavā dhruvam .. 143 ..
4.23.d:
दुर्वासा उवाच ॥
अतिशापः प्रसादो वा भवेद्दैवेन दानव ॥
सत्कीर्तिरपकीर्तिर्वा प्राक्तनप्रभवा ध्रुवम् ॥ 143 ॥
4.23.m:
"A severe curse or grace comes about by fate, O Dānava;
good fame or ill fame surely arises from past deeds. // 143

4.23.s:
viṣṇubhaktabaleḥ putraḥ sadvaṃśaprabhavo
janaḥ .. janakādviṣṇubhakto'si jānāmi tvāṃ suniścitam .. 144 ..
4.23.d:
विष्णुभक्तबलेः पुत्रः सद्वंशप्रभवो
जनः ॥ जनकाद्विष्णुभक्तोऽसि जानामि त्वां सुनिश्चितम् ॥ 144 ॥
4.23.m: You are the son of Bali, a devotee of Viṣṇu, born of an excellent lineage. / From your father you are a devotee of Viṣṇu; I know this for certain. // 144

4.23.s:
janakasya svabhāvo hi janye tiṣṭhati niścitam ..
yathā śrīkṛṣṇapādāṅkaḥ kālīyavaṃśamastake .. 145 ..
4.23.d:
जनकस्य स्वभावो हि जन्ये तिष्ठति निश्चितम् ॥
यथा श्रीकृष्णपादाङ्कः कालीयवंशमस्तके ॥ 145 ॥
4.23.m: just as the footprint of glorious Kṛṣṇa is on the head of Kālīya’s race. // 145

4.23.s:
saṃprāpya gārdabhīṃ yoniṃ vatsa nirvāṇatāṃ vraja ..
pūrvaṃ kṛṣṇārcanaphalaṃ na hi luptaṃ satāṃ cirāt .. 146 ..
4.23.d:
संप्राप्य गार्दभीं योनिं वत्स निर्वाणतां व्रज ॥
पूर्वं कृष्णार्चनफलं न हि लुप्तं सतां चिरात् ॥ 146 ॥
4.23.m:
Attaining birth as a donkey, my child, go to liberation;
for the fruit of prior worship of Kṛṣṇa is never lost to the virtuous even after a long time. // 146

4.23.s:
vṛndāraṇyaṃ tālavanaṃ vraja śīghraṃ vrajāntikam ..
prāṇāṃstyaktvā hareścakrānmuktiṃ prāpsyasi niścitam .. 147 ..
4.23.d:
वृन्दारण्यं तालवनं व्रज शीघ्रं व्रजान्तिकम् ॥
प्राणांस्त्यक्त्वा हरेश्चक्रान्मुक्तिं प्राप्स्यसि निश्चितम् ॥ 147 ॥
4.23.m:
Go quickly to Vṛndāraṇya, to the Tāla forest near Vraja;
leaving your life-breaths by Hari's discus, you will surely attain release. // 147

4.23.s:
tilottame bhārate tvaṃ bāṇaputrī bhaviṣyasi ..
śrīkṛṣṇapautraśleṣeṇa punaḥ pūtā bhaviṣyasi .. 148 ..
4.23.d:
तिलोत्तमे भारते त्वं बाणपुत्री भविष्यसि ॥
श्रीकृष्णपौत्रश्लेषेण पुनः पूता भविष्यसि ॥ 148 ॥
4.23.m:
O Tilottamā, in Bhārata you will become the daughter of Bāṇa;
through the embrace of glorious Kṛṣṇa's grandson, you will become pure once again." // 148

4.23.s:
ityevamuktvā sa munirvirarāma mahāmune ..
tau jagmaturyathāsthānaṃ praṇamya munipuṃgavam .. 149 ..
4.23.d:
इत्येवमुक्त्वा स मुनिर्विरराम महामुने ॥
तौ जग्मतुर्यथास्थानं प्रणम्य मुनिपुंगवम् ॥ 149 ॥
4.23.m:
Having spoken thus, that sage paused, O great sage;
having bowed to the bull among sages, the two went to their respective places. // 149

4.23.s:
ityuktaṃ sarvavṛttāntaṃ daityasya kharajanmanaḥ ..
tilottamā bāṇaputrī hyuṣā'niruddhakāminī .. 4.23.150 ..
4.23.d:
इत्युक्तं सर्ववृत्तान्तं दैत्यस्य खरजन्मनः ॥
तिलोत्तमा बाणपुत्री ह्युषाऽनिरुद्धकामिनी ॥ 4.23.150 ॥
4.23.m:
Thus the entire narrative of the demon born as an ass has been told;
and Tilottamā was indeed Bāṇa's daughter, Uṣā, the beloved of Aniruddha. // 4.23.150
